+@REM "License"); you may not use this file except in compliance
+@REM with the License.  You may obtain a copy of the License at
+@REM
+@REM    http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0
+@REM
+@REM Unless required by applicable law or agreed to in writing,
+@REM software distributed under the License is distributed on an
+@REM "AS IS" BASIS, WITHOUT WARRANTIES OR CONDITIONS OF ANY
+@REM KIND, either express or implied.  See the License for the
+@REM specific language governing permissions and limitations
+@REM under the License.
+@REM ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@REM ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+@REM Apache Maven Wrapper startup batch script, version 3.3.4
+@REM
+@REM Optional ENV vars
+@REM   MVNW_REPOURL - repo url base for downloading maven distribution
+@REM   MVNW_USERNAME/MVNW_PASSWORD - user and password for downloading maven
+@REM   MVNW_VERBOSE - true: enable verbose log; others: silence the output
+@REM ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+@IF "%__MVNW_ARG0_NAME__%"=="" (SET __MVNW_ARG0_NAME__=%~nx0)
+@SET __MVNW_CMD__=
+@SET __MVNW_ERROR__=
+@SET __MVNW_PSMODULEP_SAVE=%PSModulePath%
+@SET PSModulePath=
+@FOR /F "usebackq tokens=1* delims==" %%A IN (`powershell -noprofile "& {$scriptDir='%~dp0'; $script='%__MVNW_ARG0_NAME__%'; icm -ScriptBlock ([Scriptblock]::Create((Get-Content -Raw '%~f0'))) -NoNewScope}"`) DO @(
+  IF "%%A"=="MVN_CMD" (set __MVNW_CMD__=%%B) ELSE IF "%%B"=="" (echo %%A) ELSE (echo %%A=%%B)
+)
+@SET PSModulePath=%__MVNW_PSMODULEP_SAVE%
+@SET __MVNW_PSMODULEP_SAVE=
+@SET __MVNW_ARG0_NAME__=
+@SET MVNW_USERNAME=
+@SET MVNW_PASSWORD=
+@IF NOT "%__MVNW_CMD__%"=="" ("%__MVNW_CMD__%" %*)
+@echo Cannot start maven from wrapper >&2 && exit /b 1
+@GOTO :EOF
+: end batch / begin powershell #>
+
+$ErrorActionPreference = "Stop"
+if ($env:MVNW_VERBOSE -eq "true") {
+  $VerbosePreference = "Continue"
+}
+
+# calculate distributionUrl, requires .mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties
+$distributionUrl = (Get-Content -Raw "$scriptDir/.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties" | ConvertFrom-StringData).distributionUrl
+if (!$distributionUrl) {
+  Write-Error "cannot read distributionUrl property in $scriptDir/.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties"
+}
+
+switch -wildcard -casesensitive ( $($distributionUrl -replace '^.*/','') ) {
+  "maven-mvnd-*" {
+    $USE_MVND = $true
+    $distributionUrl = $distributionUrl -replace '-bin\.[^.]*$',"-windows-amd64.zip"
+    $MVN_CMD = "mvnd.cmd"
+    break
+  }
+  default {
+    $USE_MVND = $false
+    $MVN_CMD = $script -replace '^mvnw','mvn'
+    break
+  }
+}
+
+# apply MVNW_REPOURL and calculate MAVEN_HOME
+# maven home pattern: ~/.m2/wrapper/dists/{apache-maven-<version>,maven-mvnd-<version>-<platform>}/<hash>
+if ($env:MVNW_REPOURL) {
+  $MVNW_REPO_PATTERN = if ($USE_MVND -eq $False) { "/org/apache/maven/" } else { "/maven/mvnd/" }
+  $distributionUrl = "$env:MVNW_REPOURL$MVNW_REPO_PATTERN$($distributionUrl -replace "^.*$MVNW_REPO_PATTERN",'')"
+}
+$distributionUrlName = $distributionUrl -replace '^.*/',''
+$distributionUrlNameMain = $distributionUrlName -replace '\.[^.]*$','' -replace '-bin$',''
+
+$MAVEN_M2_PATH = "$HOME/.m2"
+if ($env:MAVEN_USER_HOME) {
+  $MAVEN_M2_PATH = "$env:MAVEN_USER_HOME"
+}
+
+if (-not (Test-Path -Path $MAVEN_M2_PATH)) {
+    New-Item -Path $MAVEN_M2_PATH -ItemType Directory | Out-Null
+}
+
+$MAVEN_WRAPPER_DISTS = $null
+if ((Get-Item $MAVEN_M2_PATH).Target[0] -eq $null) {
+  $MAVEN_WRAPPER_DISTS = "$MAVEN_M2_PATH/wrapper/dists"
+} else {
+  $MAVEN_WRAPPER_DISTS = (Get-Item $MAVEN_M2_PATH).Target[0] + "/wrapper/dists"
+}
+
+$MAVEN_HOME_PARENT = "$MAVEN_WRAPPER_DISTS/$distributionUrlNameMain"
+$MAVEN_HOME_NAME = ([System.Security.Cryptography.SHA256]::Create().ComputeHash([byte[]][char[]]$distributionUrl) | ForEach-Object {$_.ToString("x2")}) -join ''
+$MAVEN_HOME = "$MAVEN_HOME_PARENT/$MAVEN_HOME_NAME"
+
+if (Test-Path -Path "$MAVEN_HOME" -PathType Container) {
+  Write-Verbose "found existing MAVEN_HOME at $MAVEN_HOME"
+  Write-Output "MVN_CMD=$MAVEN_HOME/bin/$MVN_CMD"
+  exit $?
+}
+
+if (! $distributionUrlNameMain -or ($distributionUrlName -eq $distributionUrlNameMain)) {
+  Write-Error "distributionUrl is not valid, must end with *-bin.zip, but found $distributionUrl"
+}
+
+# prepare tmp dir
+$TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR_HOLDER = New-TemporaryFile
+$TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR = New-Item -Itemtype Directory -Path "$TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR_HOLDER.dir"
+$TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR_HOLDER.Delete() | Out-Null
+trap {
+  if ($TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR.Exists) {
+    try { Remove-Item $TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR -Recurse -Force | Out-Null }
+    catch { Write-Warning "Cannot remove $TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR" }
+  }
+}
+
+New-Item -Itemtype Directory -Path "$MAVEN_HOME_PARENT" -Force | Out-Null
+
+# Download and Install Apache Maven
+Write-Verbose "Couldn't find MAVEN_HOME, downloading and installing it ..."
+Write-Verbose "Downloading from: $distributionUrl"
+Write-Verbose "Downloading to: $TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR/$distributionUrlName"
+
+$webclient = New-Object System.Net.WebClient
+if ($env:MVNW_USERNAME -and $env:MVNW_PASSWORD) {
+  $webclient.Credentials = New-Object System.Net.NetworkCredential($env:MVNW_USERNAME, $env:MVNW_PASSWORD)
+}
+[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12
+$webclient.DownloadFile($distributionUrl, "$TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR/$distributionUrlName") | Out-Null
+
+# If specified, validate the SHA-256 sum of the Maven distribution zip file
+$distributionSha256Sum = (Get-Content -Raw "$scriptDir/.mvn/wrapper/maven-wrapper.properties" | ConvertFrom-StringData).distributionSha256Sum
+if ($distributionSha256Sum) {
+  if ($USE_MVND) {
+    Write-Error "Checksum validation is not supported for maven-mvnd. `nPlease disable validation by removing 'distributionSha256Sum' from your maven-wrapper.properties."
+  }
+  Import-Module $PSHOME\Modules\Microsoft.PowerShell.Utility -Function Get-FileHash
+  if ((Get-FileHash "$TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR/$distributionUrlName" -Algorithm SHA256).Hash.ToLower() -ne $distributionSha256Sum) {
+    Write-Error "Error: Failed to validate Maven distribution SHA-256, your Maven distribution might be compromised. If you updated your Maven version, you need to update the specified distributionSha256Sum property."
+  }
+}
+
+# unzip and move
+Expand-Archive "$TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR/$distributionUrlName" -DestinationPath "$TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR" | Out-Null
+
+# Find the actual extracted directory name (handles snapshots where filename != directory name)
+$actualDistributionDir = ""
+
+# First try the expected directory name (for regular distributions)
+$expectedPath = Join-Path "$TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR" "$distributionUrlNameMain"
+$expectedMvnPath = Join-Path "$expectedPath" "bin/$MVN_CMD"
+if ((Test-Path -Path $expectedPath -PathType Container) -and (Test-Path -Path $expectedMvnPath -PathType Leaf)) {
+  $actualDistributionDir = $distributionUrlNameMain
+}
+
+# If not found, search for any directory with the Maven executable (for snapshots)
+if (!$actualDistributionDir) {
+  Get-ChildItem -Path "$TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR" -Directory | ForEach-Object {
+    $testPath = Join-Path $_.FullName "bin/$MVN_CMD"
+    if (Test-Path -Path $testPath -PathType Leaf) {
+      $actualDistributionDir = $_.Name
+    }
+  }
+}
+
+if (!$actualDistributionDir) {
+  Write-Error "Could not find Maven distribution directory in extracted archive"
+}
+
+Write-Verbose "Found extracted Maven distribution directory: $actualDistributionDir"
+Rename-Item -Path "$TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR/$actualDistributionDir" -NewName $MAVEN_HOME_NAME | Out-Null
+try {
+  Move-Item -Path "$TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR/$MAVEN_HOME_NAME" -Destination $MAVEN_HOME_PARENT | Out-Null
+} catch {
+  if (! (Test-Path -Path "$MAVEN_HOME" -PathType Container)) {
+    Write-Error "fail to move MAVEN_HOME"
+  }
+} finally {
+  try { Remove-Item $TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR -Recurse -Force | Out-Null }
+  catch { Write-Warning "Cannot remove $TMP_DOWNLOAD_DIR" }
+}
+
+Write-Output "MVN_CMD=$MAVEN_HOME/bin/$MVN_CMD"

@@ -1,68 +1,68 @@
 package dev.pathland.demo.qt
 
 import com.sun.jna.Memory
 import dev.pathland.demo.DemoTheme
 import dev.pathland.demo.assets.DemoAssets
 import dev.pathland.demo.desktop.RingEventReader
 import dev.pathland.demo.music.MusicPlayerView
 import dev.pathland.view.core.Environment
-import dev.pathland.view.core.ffm.PathlandCore
-import dev.pathland.view.core.ffm.RingOpcodeSink
+import dev.pathland.nativecore.PathlandCore
+import dev.pathland.nativecore.RingOpcodeSink
 import dev.pathland.view.core.signal.Signals
 import dev.pathland.view.core.state.InMemoryStateStore
 import dev.pathland.view.core.state.PersistentState
 import dev.pathland.view.engine.Emitter
 import dev.pathland.view.engine.InputDispatcher
 
 /**
  * Runs the shared Kotlin [MusicPlayerView] under the native Qt Quick renderer.
  *
  * The Kotlin DSL mounts the view through the fine-grained [Emitter] into a
  * `libpathland_core` shared ring ([RingOpcodeSink], zero-copy). The in-process
  * Qt renderer pumps the same ring in place (`pathland_qt_run_ring`); native
  * inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that this host drains and dispatches
  * through [InputDispatcher] into the app's bindings.
  *
  * No Swing, no Qt API — only Pathland authoring.
  */
 object QtHost {
 
     /** Max events drained per wake (× 16 bytes each). */
     private const val MAX_EVENTS = 64
     private const val WINDOW_WIDTH = 1180
     private const val WINDOW_HEIGHT = 800
 
     @JvmStatic
     fun main(args: Array<String>) {
         val core = PathlandCore.instance()
         RingOpcodeSink(core).use { sink ->
             val handle = sink.handle()
 
             // The session's state + theme, exactly as the server session seeds them.
             val state = PersistentState(InMemoryStateStore(), "desktop")
             // A placeholder host path signal: MusicPlayerView has no router.
             val activePath = Signals.signal("/")
 
             val emitter = Emitter(sink, DemoTheme.adaptive())
             val result = emitter.mount(MusicPlayerView.make(), Environment(state))
             val dispatcher = InputDispatcher(result, activePath)
             val reader = RingEventReader(core.ringPtr(handle), core.ringLen(handle))
 
             // Wake callback: drain raw EVENT opcodes and route them into the app's
             // bindings. Re-emission happens on the Qt main thread, the only writer.
             val onEvent = QtRendererNative.EventCallback {
                 val buf = Memory(MAX_EVENTS.toLong() * 16)
                 val n = core.drainEvents(handle, buf, MAX_EVENTS)
                 if (n > 0) {
                     dispatcher.dispatch(reader.decode(buf.getByteArray(0, n * 16)))
                 }
             }
 
             val renderer = QtRendererNative.instance()
             renderer.setAssetRoot(DemoAssets.extractToTemp().toString())
 
             // Blocks until the window closes; the ring (handle) must outlive it.
             renderer.runRing(core.ringMut(handle), onEvent, WINDOW_WIDTH, WINDOW_HEIGHT)
         }
     }
 }

 # pathland-desktop-demo — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 5, 2026
 
 Runs the shared Kotlin `MusicPlayerView` (`dev.pathland.demo.music` from
 `pathland-demo-views-kotlin`) under the **native GTK4 renderer**
 (`libpathland_gtk`, `dev.pathland.demo.gtk.GtkHost`) or the **Qt Quick renderer**
 (`libpathland_qt`, `dev.pathland.demo.qt.QtHost`) — the cross-language,
 shared-renderer story. Protocol contract: `spec/`.
 
 ## How it works
 
 - The Kotlin DSL mounts the view through its fine-grained `Emitter` into a
-  `libpathland_core` shared ring (`RingOpcodeSink`, **zero-copy**).
+  `libpathland_core` shared ring (`RingOpcodeSink` from `pathland-native-core`,
+  **zero-copy**).
 - The in-process renderer pumps the same ring in place
   (`pathland_gtk_run_ring` / `pathland_qt_run_ring`); no
   `pathland-view-native` host is involved.
 - Native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes that the host drains
   (`pathland_core_drain_events`) and dispatches into the app's bindings via the
   shared `InputDispatcher` (taps, text/value/date inputs, **media events**,
   router back).
 - State/theme/platform seeding mirrors the server session: `PersistentState`
   over an `InMemoryStateStore`, `DemoTheme.adaptive()` as the emitter theme.
 - **App-driven media**: the renderer plays the demo's tracks and reports
   `MEDIA_*` events back through the ring. The app's web-style
   `/_pathland/assets/...` paths resolve against a local asset root: the demo
   extracts its audio + covers from the shared `pathland-demo-views-kotlin` jar
   at startup (`DemoAssets.extractToTemp`) and calls the renderer's
   `set_asset_root`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **`GtkRendererNative`** — JNA binding to `libpathland_gtk`
   (`pathland_gtk_run_ring` + `pathland_gtk_set_asset_root`); library resolved
   from `pathland.gtk.lib` or `java.library.path`.
 - **`QtRendererNative`** — JNA binding to `libpathland_qt`
   (`pathland_qt_run_ring` + `pathland_qt_set_asset_root`); library resolved
   from `pathland.qt.lib` or `java.library.path`.
 - **`RingEventReader`** (shared, `dev.pathland.demo.desktop`) — decodes raw ring
   `EVENT` opcodes into `dev.pathland.view.core.transport.Event`, resolving
   `TEXT_CHANGED`/`NAVIGATE` strings from the shared host → guest event arena
   (header `0x40`), plus `MEDIA_*` and `FIT_CHANGED` (routed to the emitter's fit
   sink, so the `SizeThatFits` slot swaps to its wide candidate).
 - **`GtkHost`** (`main`) — Java host; mounts the Apple Music-style player,
   extracts the demo assets, runs GTK (1180×800), drains and dispatches events.
 - **`QtHost`** (`main`) — Kotlin host; mounts the player, extracts the demo
   assets, runs Qt Quick, drains and dispatches events.
 - The `Emitter` sets `BINDING_ID` on bound controls for `RingOpcodeSink`s (the
   GTK renderer gates `TEXT_CHANGED`/`VALUE_CHANGED` on it).
 
 ## Not implemented / gaps
 
 - **GTK playback requires GStreamer** with the mp3 decoding plugins installed;
   without it the app runs but the pipeline errors on play.
 - The GTK renderer's `attach_control_events` covers `TOGGLE`/`SLIDER`/
   `TEXT_FIELD`/`PICKER` only: `DATE_PICKER`, `STEPPER`, `COLOR_PICKER`, and
   `TEXT_EDITOR` render but do not (yet) emit events under GTK.
 - Qt6 dev libraries are required to build/run the Qt renderer.
 - macOS requires `-XstartOnFirstThread` for both hosts.
 - No automated GUI test (headless renderer tests live in the Rust crates).
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test -pl pathland-desktop-demo` — `RingEventReaderTest` (headless, no GTK/Qt;
 pointer/value/date/text/navigate/media/fit decoding and bounds behaviour).
 Manual: `scripts/run-java-gtk-demo.sh` and `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`.

@@ -0,0 +1,141 @@
+package dev.pathland.nativecore
+
+import com.sun.jna.Library
+import com.sun.jna.Memory
+import com.sun.jna.Native
+import com.sun.jna.Pointer
+import dev.pathland.view.core.protocol.Opcode
+import java.io.File
+import java.util.Locale
+
+/** JNA binding to the Rust `libpathland_core` cdylib (SPSC ring + opcode engine). */
+class PathlandCore private constructor() {
+
+    /** Thrown when the native library cannot be linked. */
+    class NativeUnavailableException(message: String, cause: Throwable?) :
+        IllegalStateException(message, cause)
+
+    private interface NativePathlandCore : Library {
+        fun pathland_core_create(): Pointer
+        fun pathland_core_destroy(handle: Pointer)
+        fun pathland_ring_buffer_push(handle: Pointer, opcode: Pointer): Boolean
+        fun pathland_core_arena_alloc(handle: Pointer, bytes: Pointer, len: Int): Int
+        fun pathland_core_begin_frame(handle: Pointer)
+        fun pathland_core_end_frame(handle: Pointer)
+        fun pathland_core_frame_count(handle: Pointer): Int
+        fun pathland_core_ring_ptr(handle: Pointer): Pointer
+        fun pathland_core_ring_len(handle: Pointer): Long
+        fun pathland_core_ring_mut(handle: Pointer): Pointer
+        fun pathland_core_drain_events(handle: Pointer, out: Pointer, max: Int): Int
+        fun pathland_core_send_event(handle: Pointer, opcode: Pointer): Boolean
+    }
+
+    private val nativeCore: NativePathlandCore
+
+    /** Reused 16-byte opcode buffer (zero per-op heap allocations). */
+    private val opcodeBuf = Memory(Opcode.SIZE.toLong())
+
+    init {
+        try {
+            val libraryPath = resolveLibraryPath()
+                ?: throw NativeUnavailableException(
+                    "libpathland_core not found on java.library.path; " +
+                        "set the system property pathland.core.lib to its full path",
+                    null,
+                )
+            nativeCore = Native.load(libraryPath, NativePathlandCore::class.java)
+        } catch (e: NativeUnavailableException) {
+            throw e
+        } catch (t: Throwable) {
+            throw NativeUnavailableException("failed to link libpathland_core", t)
+        }
+    }
+
+    // --- ring host lifetime ---
+
+    /** Create a ring host over a fresh shared ring. */
+    fun create(): Pointer = nativeCore.pathland_core_create()
+
+    /** Destroy a ring host. */
+    fun destroy(handle: Pointer) {
+        nativeCore.pathland_core_destroy(handle)
+    }
+
+    // --- guest → host ring ---
+
+    /** Push one 16-byte opcode into the shared ring. Returns false when full. */
+    fun push(handle: Pointer, opcode: ByteArray): Boolean {
+        opcodeBuf.write(0, opcode, 0, Opcode.SIZE)
+        return nativeCore.pathland_ring_buffer_push(handle, opcodeBuf)
+    }
+
+    /** Allocate bytes into the bump arena, returning the absolute offset. */
+    fun arenaAlloc(handle: Pointer, bytes: ByteArray): Int {
+        val buf = Memory(maxOf(1, bytes.size).toLong())
+        if (bytes.isNotEmpty()) {
+            buf.write(0, bytes, 0, bytes.size)
+        }
+        return nativeCore.pathland_core_arena_alloc(handle, buf, bytes.size)
+    }
+
+    fun beginFrame(handle: Pointer) {
+        nativeCore.pathland_core_begin_frame(handle)
+    }
+
+    fun endFrame(handle: Pointer) {
+        nativeCore.pathland_core_end_frame(handle)
+    }
+
+    fun frameCount(handle: Pointer): Int = nativeCore.pathland_core_frame_count(handle)
+
+    /** Pointer to the shared linear memory (header | ring | arena). */
+    fun ringPtr(handle: Pointer): Pointer = nativeCore.pathland_core_ring_ptr(handle)
+
+    /** Byte length of the shared linear memory. */
+    fun ringLen(handle: Pointer): Long = nativeCore.pathland_core_ring_len(handle)
+
+    /** Borrow the underlying shared ring for a same-process consumer. */
+    fun ringMut(handle: Pointer): Pointer = nativeCore.pathland_core_ring_mut(handle)
+
+    // --- events (host → guest) ---
+
+    /** Drain pending EVENT opcodes into [out]; returns the number written. */
+    fun drainEvents(handle: Pointer, out: Pointer, max: Int): Int =
+        nativeCore.pathland_core_drain_events(handle, out, max)
+
+    /** Push one 16-byte EVENT opcode into the host → guest event ring. */
+    fun sendEvent(handle: Pointer, opcode: ByteArray): Boolean {
+        opcodeBuf.write(0, opcode, 0, Opcode.SIZE)
+        return nativeCore.pathland_core_send_event(handle, opcodeBuf)
+    }
+
+    companion object {
+        private object Holder {
+            val INSTANCE = PathlandCore()
+        }
+
+        /** The process-wide binding; lazily links `libpathland_core` on first call. */
+        @JvmStatic
+        fun instance(): PathlandCore = Holder.INSTANCE
+
+        /** Resolve the native library's full path. */
+        fun resolveLibraryPath(): String? {
+            val override = System.getProperty("pathland.core.lib")
+            if (override != null) return override
+            val fileName = "libpathland_core" + platformLibraryExtension()
+            val libraryPath = System.getProperty("java.library.path") ?: return null
+            for (dir in libraryPath.split(File.pathSeparator)) {
+                val candidate = File(dir, fileName)
+                if (candidate.isFile) return candidate.absolutePath
+            }
+            return null
+        }
+
+        private fun platformLibraryExtension(): String {
+            val os = System.getProperty("os.name", "").lowercase(Locale.ROOT)
+            if (os.contains("mac")) return ".dylib"
+            if (os.contains("win")) return ".dll"
+            return ".so"
+        }
+    }
+}

+# pathland-native-core — implementation status
+
+**Last updated:** November 8, 2026
+
+Opt-in JNA interop for native desktop hosts. Kept in its own module so
+`pathland-view-core` (and therefore every server runtime and GraalVM
+native-image build) never carries JNA.
+
+## Implemented
+
+- **`PathlandCore`** (`dev.pathland.nativecore`): lazy JNA binding to the Rust
+  `libpathland_core` cdylib — ring host lifetime, opcode push, arena allocation,
+  frame boundaries, shared ring access, and event drain/send. Resolves the
+  library from `pathland.core.lib` or `java.library.path`.
+- **`RingOpcodeSink`** (`dev.pathland.nativecore`): zero-copy `OpcodeSink` that
+  writes 16-byte opcodes into the Rust SPSC ring through `PathlandCore`,
+  including arena-backed strings, design-token paths, float lists, attributed
+  text, dates, and theme/window metadata.
+
+## Consumers
+
+- `pathland-desktop-demo` (GTK and Qt hosts) — the only in-repo consumer.
+- External native hosts that drive `libpathland_core` directly.
+
+## Not implemented / gaps
+
+- No automated test loads the native library (it is built by `scripts/lib.sh`
+  for the desktop demos); the module is compile/test-compile clean without it.

 # --- HSTS (whole-origin, app-owned) --------------------------------------------
 # The extension deliberately does not default HSTS: it pins the entire origin
 # (all paths/ports, and subdomains with includeSubDomains) in the browser. This
 # demo is served only over HTTPS behind Render's TLS terminator, so opt in here.
 # Drop includeSubDomains if any subdomain may remain on plain HTTP; only add
 # preload if the domain is intentionally submitted to the HSTS preload list.
 quarkus.http.header."Strict-Transport-Security".value=max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains
 
 # --- Same-server proxy demo (spec/PROXY.md) ------------------------------------
 # The music player at / embeds the small ad app mounted at /ad (this same server)
 # as a sponsored slot in its Now Playing pane, via a ProxyView. This is the origin
 # app's base URL the player proxies; point it at another host/port to proxy a
 # remote app instead.
 pathland.demo.ad-url=http://localhost:8080/ad
 
 # --- Per-window id on the first request (issue #155) ---------------------------
 # Opt the DOM client into the service worker that attaches the per-window id to
 # top-level navigations, so the SSR renders the right persisted-state scope on the
 # FIRST paint (instead of defaults that the live connection then corrects). The id
 # never appears in the URL. Off by default; the worker is served at /_pathland/sw.js
 # with Service-Worker-Allowed: / (root scope) and no-cache.
 pathland.service-worker=true

+# and is served by Quarkus's static handler. The demo's media/icons are served

 # pathland-quarkus — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 7, 2026
 
 Quarkus extension for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding this extension + a
 `PathlandApp` CDI bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at
 their own subpaths (the BFF layout). Author the root view with
 `pathland-view-core`'s Kotlin DSL; Java hosts return Kotlin views from a
 `PathlandApp` bean. The extension also provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin`
 capability and pulls in `quarkus-kotlin`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Security defaults (issue #63)**: the deployment module contributes
   overridable runtime defaults via `RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem`:
   `quarkus.http.cors.enabled=true` (no origins → same-origin, which covers
   WebSocket upgrades because the CORS filter runs before routes),
   `quarkus.websockets-next.server.max-message-size`/`max-frame-size=65536`, and
   CSP + `X-Content-Type-Options`/`Referrer-Policy`/`X-Frame-Options` headers via
   `quarkus.http.header.*`. See `docs/HARDENING.md` for overrides, CSP rollout,
   reverse-proxy/TLS guidance, and edge rate limiting. The `wid` handshake query
   is validated by server-core (`WindowIds`). **HSTS is deliberately not an
   extension default** — it is a whole-origin, persistent browser policy that
   also covers other apps on the same server, so it is owned by the application
   or edge; the Quarkus demo opts in via `application.properties`.
   `docs/HARDENING.md` documents the directives and override guidance.

   `enable-forwarded-host` to `true`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS (Render, Fly,

   SSR canonical URL with zero configuration. These are lowest-priority defaults;
   application config (including

   (`host.signalHub()`: root mount, else the first mount) for external UI updates.
   `TopicSubscriptionsTest` mounts a `/topics` app and proves a background-thread
   publish reaches only the session subscribed for that subject.

   `newRoot()` returns a Kotlin-authored fixture view; the multi-session
   WebSocket tests prove SSR + live deltas work through that mount.

   from `UriInfo` and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
   `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first

   `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.

   per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from
   the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the
   `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default
   to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection
   ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters
   live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the
   shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared
   one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session).

   the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment.
   Same stateless rule as the root socket.

   dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped);
   SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS);
   per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are
   served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global
   `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS.

+  dom-renderer-<hash>.js` + the `dom-renderer.current` pointer + the service worker), so
+  a consuming application adds the extension and needs no static resources of its own;
+  the mounted-base `frameworkFile` path resolves the app's classpath copy first (TCCL),
+  then the extension jar, and adds `immutable` caching for the content-hashed bundle. A

+  handler is unavailable (it normally wins).

   `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.

   it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`)
   to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at
   `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`.

   registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over
   Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured
   max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection). The script is
   resolved through the thread-context classloader first, then the extension's own
   loader, then the system loader: extension runtime classes live in Quarkus's base
   runtime classloader and cannot see the application's `META-INF/resources` copy. The
   extension jar bundles the worker as a fallback (the TS copy script writes it), and

   `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the
   registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and

   the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the
   host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear
   at `/q/metrics`.

   Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued),
   and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM
   client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an
   "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a
   `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection /
   a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would
   otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection
   sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm
   through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive
   scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it).

   dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md
   §Transport heartbeat.

   no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious
   "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection
   that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel
   (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is
   **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't
   false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly
   (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed).

+- **Native image support** — the deployment module registers the renderer-owned

   runtime provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus` capability. The runtime has no
   dependency on the authoring DSL. Tests use Kotlin-authored fixture views to prove

 # pathland-spring-boot-starter — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 7, 2026
 
 Spring Boot auto-configuration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding the starter dependency + a
 `PathlandApp` bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own
 subpaths (the BFF layout).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Security hardening (issue #63)**: the WebSocket handlers no longer hardcode
   `setAllowedOrigins("*")`. The default is Spring's same-origin handshake check
   (the WebSocket CSRF control); cross-origin hosts must be listed explicitly in
   `pathland.allowed-origins` (comma-separated). The handshake `wid` is validated
   by server-core (`WindowIds`). SSR inherits SRI (`integrity="sha384-…"`) from
   `PathlandSession`. CSP/security headers and transport limits are documented in
   `docs/HARDENING.md` (Quarkus supplies secure defaults; Spring apps add them
   through Spring Security/server configuration).
 - **Hosted deployments work by default (issue #45 follow-up)**: a
   lowest-precedence `EnvironmentPostProcessor` contributes
   `server.forward-headers-strategy=framework`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS gets a
   correct WebSocket same-origin check and external SSR canonical URL with zero
   configuration. An explicit `server.forward-headers-strategy` in application
   config always wins (`ForwardedHeaderOverrideTest` pins this).
 - **Topic hub bean**: `PathlandAutoConfiguration` produces a `PathlandSignalHub`
   bean (`host.signalHub()`: root mount, else the first mount) for external UI
   updates. `TopicSubscriptionsTest` mounts a `/topics` app and proves a
   background-thread publish reaches only the session subscribed for that subject.
 - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `KotlinViewMountTest` proves a Java-only
   `@SpringBootApplication` bean returning `PathlandApp` mounts a Kotlin-authored
   fixture view, renders it through SSR, and receives a live signal delta.
 
 - **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
 - **SEO document head (issue #45)**: the SSR controller derives the canonical
   URL from the request and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
   `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first
   paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via
   `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.
 
 - **`PathlandAutoConfiguration`** (`@AutoConfiguration`, `@EnableWebSocket` since Spring
   Boot 3.5 no longer auto-enables it) + `META-INF/spring/…/AutoConfiguration.imports`:
   - default `StateStore` bean (`@ConditionalOnMissingBean` — Redis-or-in-memory),
   - `PathlandHost` bean (shut down with the context): every `MountedApp` bean plus the
     lone `PathlandApp` bean mounted at `/` (unless an explicit `MountedApp` claims the
     root). Without any app the host is empty and the starter is inert.
   - a `WebSocketConfigurer` registering **one handler per app** at its framework base
     (`/_pathland/ws` for the root, `/{mount}/_pathland/ws` otherwise). Each connection
     gets a fresh `uiId` (its UI model) + the client's `wid` (per-window state scope)
     from the WS `?wid=` query param (kept in `sessionStorage`, never in the page URL),
   - `PathlandIndexController` (SSR catch-all dispatching to the longest-mount app with
     the prefix stripped + a framework static controller serving the bundle + asset mount
     from `classpath:/static/_pathland/**` at both `/_pathland/**` and `/{app}/_pathland/**`;
     the more-specific mapping beats `/{*path}`, and the `!Upgrade` header excludes WS).
+    **The starter jar ships the DOM client bundle** (`static/_pathland/dom-renderer-<hash>.js`
+    + the `dom-renderer.current` pointer + the service worker), so a consuming application
+    adds the dependency and needs no static resources of its own; an app-supplied
+    `static/_pathland` copy still wins by classpath order.
     When no static file matches, the controller serves renderer-owned assets from the
     shared Rust renderer: the content-hashed base stylesheet
     (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
     `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and
     `/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg` glyphs (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` →
     `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header — no static CSS/icon
     files on any host, and a host can still override either with a file. SSR links
     the CSS via `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
     The framework controller honors byte-range requests (`206 Partial Content` +
     `Content-Range`, `416` for unsatisfiable ranges, `Accept-Ranges` on the full
     response) — a `<video>` (a `MediaController`'s playback) seeking beyond its
     buffer issues a `Range`
     request, and answering it with a full `200` would make browsers restart the media
     at byte 0.
     SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS).
 - **SSR debug comments**: the host reads the `pathland.debug-html` property
   (`@Value("${pathland.debug-html:false}")`) and forwards it to each registry, enabling
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output when set.
 - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `pathland.service-worker`
   (default `false`) forwards to the host; the SSR emits `data-pathland-service-worker`
   and the controller serves `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` +
   `Cache-Control: no-cache` (a stable, uncached script the browser byte-compares).
 - **`SpringConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketSession` to `PathlandConnection`.
   `AutoCloseable`: a failed send surfaces as a close (the session's
   `closeConnection` closes the underlying session) so the DOM client reconnects +
   `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an open socket.
 - **Heartbeat** — the socket replies to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
   **at the transport layer** (through its `SpringConnection`, no actor/session
   dependency; spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat).
 - **Observability (issue #62)** — `spring-boot-starter-actuator` supplies the
   `MeterRegistry`; auto-config builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over it (decorated with
   `TracingTelemetry` when an `OpenTelemetry` bean is present — add
   `micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel` to opt in) and a `HealthIndicator` reporting the host
   UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/actuator/health`. The `pathland.*` meters are
   exposed at `/actuator/prometheus` (add `micrometer-registry-prometheus`).
 
 ## App DX
 
 ```java
 @SpringBootApplication
 public class MyApp {
     public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(MyApp.class, args); }
     @Bean PathlandApp pathlandApp() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
     @Bean MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); } // optional 2nd app
 }
 ```
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test` — `PathlandAutoConfigurationTest` (`@SpringBootTest`): a `PathlandApp` bean
 mounts at `/` and SSR renders the root. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest`
 (`@SpringBootTest(RANDOM_PORT)`) opens **100 concurrent real WS sessions** against
 `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar probe) and asserts each
 connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated, and is never closed by
 the peer. `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts
 `/actuator/health` reports the `pathland` component UP and the auto-configured
 `PathlandTelemetry` is a `MicrometerTelemetry` registering `pathland.*` meters.
 `BaseCssHeadersTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts the linked SSR
 `<link>`, the immutable `text/css` response at the global and mounted bases, and
 a 404 for an unknown hash.
 Manual: the `pathland-spring-boot-demo` renders `/`, `/kitchen`, `/settings`
 and the 404 fallback **and a second app at `/app2`**; a WebSocket handshake to
 `/_pathland/ws` and `/app2/_pathland/ws` returns 101.

 # pathland-view-core (JVM engine + DSL) — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 7, 2026
 
 The shared, framework-agnostic JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL for the
 Pathland protocol, written entirely in Kotlin. It owns the `View` SPI and shared
 authoring vocabulary, the retained-tree diff emitter,
-signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform state, JNA ring
-interop, and the `dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers.
-Server and renderer modules depend on this one module; Java hosts consume the
-Kotlin-authored views through JVM interop.
+signals/computed/effects, the wire codec, router, cross-platform state, and the
+`dev.pathland.view.dsl` SwiftUI-shaped builders/modifiers. Server and renderer
+modules depend on this one module; Java hosts consume the Kotlin-authored views
+through JVM interop. JNA ring interop lives in the opt-in
+`pathland-native-core` module, so this module (and every server/native-image
+build) carries no JNA.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Protocol** (`dev.pathland.view.core.protocol`): `Components`, `Properties`,
   `Commands` (incl. `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`), `Categories`, `ValueTypes`, `Opcode`,
   `ValueEncoder`, `WireValue`, `TokenPath`.
 - **Attributed text** (`dev.pathland.view.core.AttributedString`): pure-Kotlin
   model + range-tracking builder (Kotlin char indices → UTF-8 byte offsets) and
   payload encode/decode; `Text(AttributedString)` / `Text(Signal<AttributedString>)`
   emit `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT` through the emitter and both sinks.
 - **Built-in inline Markdown**: `Text("...")` parses the v1 subset by default
   (`**bold**`/`__bold__`, `*italic*`/`_italic_`, `` `code` ``,
   `~~strikethrough~~`, `[label](url)`); `markdown = false` renders literal text.
   `dev.pathland.markdown.Markdown` is now a **pure-Java parser** (no native
   library, so it runs on every platform and under GraalVM native-image); it is a
   behavioural port of the Rust `pathland-markdown` crate (pre-scan + bounded
   cache). The Rust crate remains the parser for the Rust DSL and non-JVM hosts.
   Plain results use the compact `SET_TEXT` path; rich results emit
   `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`. Reactive `Text(Signal<String>)` parses on change.
 - **Signals** (`dev.pathland.view.core.signal`): `signal`/`state`/`computed`/
   `effect`/`untracked`, synchronous glitch-free flush, equality suppression, error
   caching/retry, circular-dependency detection, and a thread-safe global
   `Scheduler`. `Signals.state` binds to the ambient session `PersistentState`
   during a component render.
 - **Topic subscriptions** (`dev.pathland.view.core.subscription`): a strongly
   typed `Topic<T, S>` and the DSL `topic(key, subject, initial)` (also
   `Signals.topic`). Scoped topics name an entity subject; `Topic.global(name)`
   declares an unscoped `Topic<T, GlobalSubject>` with the two-argument
   `topic(key, initial)` form. Both return a normal `Signal<T>` backed by a
   session-local mirror; the server runtime registers it with the app's hub and
   applies published values on the session actor. `SessionContext` (thread-local,
   installed by `PathlandSession` around every actor task) also exposes
   `unsubscribe` and `submit`. Resolution is lazy when a root view's field
   initializer runs before the context is installed.
 - **State** (`dev.pathland.view.core.state`): `PersistentState`, untyped
   `StateStore`, in-memory store and provider. Kotlin `Component` state delegates
   bind directly before `body()`; the Java `State` field/binder machinery and
   annotation processor are removed.
 - **Transport** (`dev.pathland.view.core.transport`): `ProtocolFrame`,
   `FrameCodec`, `Event`, `EnvironmentData`, `OpcodeSink`, `FrameOpcodeSink`.
   **Hardened (issue #63)**: `FrameCodec.parse` reads the attacker-controlled
   `opcodeCount`/`stringsLen` as unsigned `Long` values and validates them
   against the actual message length before allocating; string offsets are
   bounds-checked (`Parsed.stringAt`). A declared `opcodeCount` that overflows
   `Int` arithmetic now throws instead of triggering an OOM allocation.
 - **Router** (`dev.pathland.view.core.router`): `Route`, `RouteTable`, `Router`,
   `Navigation`, `NavigationContainer`, `NavigationIntent`, `Params`, `Chrome`,
   `NavOp`. `NavigationLink` and the navigation helpers live in the Kotlin DSL.
-- **JNA interop** (`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`): lazy `PathlandCore` binding and
-  `RingOpcodeSink` over `libpathland_core`.
+- **JNA interop**: moved to `pathland-native-core` (`dev.pathland.nativecore`),
+  so server runtimes do not pull JNA.
 - **Emitter** (`dev.pathland.view.engine`): `Emitter`, `PathlandNode`, `ViewSlot`,
   `RenderResult`, `InputDispatcher`, `ReactiveValues`, `DateInput`, `MediaInput`.
   Implements mount/id assignment, diff-based reactive emission, node-level binding
   effects, structural reconciliation, fit/media/navigation routing, and the
   zero-opcode unchanged recompute contract. A replaced child is relinked to its
   real parent (not the tree root), so a `SIZE_THAT_FITS` swap cannot detach a
   pinned root `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` or drop its media routing. Registered `MediaController`s are
   projected as pinned, non-visual root children; `unregisterMediaController`
   removes them without touching the app tree.
 - **Shared SPI/values** (`dev.pathland.view.core`): `View`, `ViewModifier`,
   `Configurable`, `ChildrenView`, `Modified`, `ViewBuilder`,
   `Environment*`, `Platform`, `Theme*`, `MediaController`, `WindowMetadata`,
   `ProxyConfig`, `Color`, `Length`, shared enums, style protocols, and modifier
   wrappers.
 - **Protocol manifest validation** (`ProtocolManifestTest`): the hand-written
   protocol constants (`Components`, `Properties`, `Commands`, `Categories`,
   `ValueTypes`) are checked against `spec/protocol.tsv` — including no extra
   public numeric constants and the full `ValueTypes.forProperty` mapping. No
   Java source is generated.
 - **Shared engine traces**: the Kotlin DSL tests run the mount/text/property
   scenarios against the Rust-emitted PLPL fixtures under `spec/engine-traces/`,
   byte-for-byte. The canonical order lives in `spec/ENGINE.md`.
 - **Tests**: `pathland-view-core` owns the signal, state, frame-codec, and
   protocol-manifest tests; Kotlin DSL tests exercise the emitter end-to-end, and
   the server/HTML/desktop consumers cover their integration paths.
 
 ## Authoring DSL (`dev.pathland.view.dsl`)
 
 - **SwiftUI-shaped builders**: `Text` (plain, `Signal<String>`, or
   `AttributedString` / `Signal<AttributedString>`), `Image`, `Icon`, `Color`,
   `Rectangle`, `Circle`, `Ellipse`, `Capsule`, `RoundedRectangle`, `Shape`,
   `Divider`, `Spacer`, `ProgressView`, `Gauge`, `Label`, `Group`.
 - **Containers**: `VStack`, `HStack`, `ZStack`, `Grid`, `GridRow`, `ScrollView`,
   `LazyVStack`, `LazyHStack`, `LazyVGrid`, `LazyHGrid`, `ViewThatFits`/`Fit`,
   `ProxyView`, `ForEach`.
 - **Controls**: `Button` (title or label subtree), `TextField`, `SecureField`,
   `TextEditor`, `Toggle`, `Slider`, `Stepper`, `DatePicker`, `Picker`, `Menu`,
   `ColorPicker`.
 - **Automatic child collection**: `VStack { Text("a"); Text("b") }` needs no
   `.children(...)`. A custom `Component` constructed inline in a block
   auto-registers; a view stored as a field is added explicitly with `+field`.
 - **Scope isolation** (`@PathlandDsl`): every view builder lambda takes a
   `PathlandScope` receiver, and `PathlandScope`, `Navigation.Builder`, and the
   modifier/style `Config` receivers carry the same `@DslMarker`. An outer
   router/config receiver therefore cannot be captured implicitly inside a
   nested view builder (e.g. `fallback(...)` inside `VStack { }` is a compile
   error). Child collection itself is unchanged — the thread-local `ViewScopes`
   stack still drives auto-registration.
 - **Signals**: `signal`, `computed`, `constant`, `effect`, `untracked`,
   `topic(key, subject, initial)`, `Signal<T>.value`, `WritableSignal<T>.value`,
   `Signal<T>.map`, `readonly`.
 - **Modifier sugar**: `.padding`, `.frame`, `.offset`, `.position`, `.fixedSize`,
   layout priority/z-index/aspect ratio, the full text-formatting surface,
   foreground/background/border/corner radius/shadow, visual effects, transforms,
   visibility/disabled/hit-testing, accessibility, tap/pointer events,
   environment binding, styles, window metadata, and navigation intents.
 - **Persisted state**: `Component` base class + `val count by state(0)`
   (auto-keyed by property name) or `state(0, "key")`; a `mutableState(0)` signal
   form for two-way controls.
 - **Reactive bodies**: plain `if`/`when`/`for` in `body()`; `ForEach` over a static
   list or `Signal<List<T>>` with row-scoped child collection.
 - **Navigation**: `navigator { route(...) }`, `NavigationStack`, `NavigationLink`,
   `isActive`, and `.navigate`/`.push`/`.replace` intents.
 - **Media**: `Video(controller)` stays where the app places it; audio remains
   view-less. `controller.register()` projects a controller at the root.
 - **Naming**: the composite base is `Component` (renamed from `KotlinView` now
   that the Java DSL is gone); see #174.
 - **Java hosting**: a Java Spring Boot / Quarkus app mounts a Kotlin view through
   the Java-friendly `PathlandApp` functional interface
   (`return () -> MusicPlayerView.make();`). Kotlin roots expose public
   constructors and/or `@JvmStatic make(...)` factories.
 
 ## Package boundary
 
 - `pathland-view-core` is one Maven module: `core`/`engine`/`dsl` are logical
   subpackages inside it, with a few deliberate intra-module references
   (`Color`/`MediaController`/`Modified` materialize `PathlandNode`). Splitting
   them into separate artifacts would require a node SPI first.
 - Production runtimes/renderers (`pathland-server-core`,
   `pathland-render-html`) depend on this module. Framework starters remain
   DSL-neutral at compile time; they mount Kotlin-authored fixture views in test
   scope.

 # @pathland/dom-renderer
 
 The **Pathland DOM renderer** — the web client. A small, vanilla-TypeScript
 hydration client (zero runtime dependencies) that:
 
 - **Hydrates** the server-rendered DOM by `data-pathland-id`.
 - **Decodes** self-contained `PLPL` opcode batches (bounds-checked) and applies
   them in place: **`STYLE` deltas** (the full property catalog — layout, text,
   styling, effects, semantic/control variants, plus `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` →
   CSS variables) and **`TREE` deltas** (create/delete/insert/remove/move —
   runtime structural updates without a full reload).
 - **Reports raw inputs** back over WebSocket as `EVENT` batches — the full event
   catalog (pointer down/move/up, key down/up, value/text/date changed, focus/
   editing, submit, scroll, wheel) — guest → host (flags `0x0000`), gated by the
   SSR `EVENT_LISTENERS` mask.
 - **Negotiates** the protocol version (mismatch → reload) and **reconnects**
   with exponential backoff.
 
 Styling is renderer-owned: the protocol stays renderer-agnostic. The SSR HTML
 carries a Tailwind-derived preflight plus a tokenized built-in design system
 (`--pl-*` CSS variables); per-node values are inline style, with literal colors
 inline and semantic design tokens as CSS variables. Native browser controls
 inherit the same preflight + design tokens through `.pathland-*` classes. The
 DOM renderer owns the bounded property → style map (`src/classes.ts`).
 
 ## Layout
 
 ```
 src/
   constants.ts   protocol constants (mirror spec/)
   plpl.ts        bounds-checked batch parse + string decode
   format.ts      f32/ARGB/date/float formatting
   elements.ts    component → DOM shell factory (TREE create)
   classes.ts     Option A style/state appliers (inline style + ARIA + CSS vars)
   apply.ts       delta application (STYLE + TREE) over the id → Node registry
   events.ts      guest → host EVENT encoders
   transport.ts   WebSocket connect/reconnect/version negotiation
   index.ts       bootstrap (hydrate + connect + listeners)
 ```
 
 ## Build & test
 
 ```bash
 npm ci
 npm test          # vitest (happy-dom): codec round-trips, TREE/STYLE apply, transport
 npm run build     # tsc --noEmit + esbuild -> dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js (IIFE, minified)
-npm run copy-to-demos   # copy the bundle into the Java demos' static dirs
+npm run copy-to-libs    # copy the bundle into the framework libraries' static dirs
 ```
 
 The per-window-id service worker has a real-browser E2E (Chromium + WebKit) — the
 worker-engine differences (e.g. WebKit reporting an empty `clientId` on navigations)
 are invisible to jsdom, so they are guarded here:
 
 ```bash
 npx playwright install chromium webkit   # one-time
 npm run test:e2e                          # boots a fixture server + the shipped sw.js
 ```
 
 ## The bundle
 
-`dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` is served by the Spring Boot and Quarkus (Java + Kotlin) demos under a
-content-hashed name — `dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` (copied into each demo's static
-resources by `npm run copy-to-demos`, which also prunes stale copies and writes the
-`dom-renderer.current` pointer manifest the SSR layer reads to emit the `<script src>`).
-The fresh URL per build busts the immutable asset cache.
+`dist/pathland-dom-renderer.js` ships in the Spring Boot starter and the Quarkus
+extension under a content-hashed name — `dom-renderer-<sha256>.js` (copied into each
+library's static resources by `npm run copy-to-libs`, which also prunes stale copies
+and writes the `dom-renderer.current` pointer manifest the SSR layer reads to emit the
+`<script src>`). Applications get the bundle automatically; the fresh URL per build
+busts the immutable asset cache.
 
 ## Transport resilience
 
 `src/transport.ts` reconnects with exponential backoff, keeps the connection
 alive with a `META::PING`/`PONG` heartbeat + no-activity watchdog, and recovers
 from lost deltas: a **sequence gap** (a batch whose per-stream `sequence` breaks
 the chain) makes the client skip the gapped batch and request a full snapshot
 (`META::RESYNC`). See `spec/OPCODE.md` §Transport heartbeat and §Sequence gap
 detection.

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.2.2</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>Pathland View</name>
    <description>
        The Pathland JVM engine, runtime and authoring DSL, written in Kotlin: the
        16-byte opcode protocol, retained-tree diff emitter, Angular-style signals,
        wire codec, router, state, lazy JNA ring interop, and the SwiftUI-shaped
        `dev.pathland.view.dsl` builders/modifiers every JVM host mounts. All server
        runtimes depend on this module. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>net.java.dev.jna</groupId>
            <artifactId>jna</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>compile</id>
                        <phase>process-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</sourceDir>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/main/java</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>test-compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/java</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                    <args>
                        <arg>-Xjvm-default=all</arg>
                    </args>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>

    <profiles>
        <!-- Maven Central requires a -javadoc.jar for every jar. This module is
             Kotlin-first (Markdown.java is the only Java source and it imports
             Kotlin classes), so the JDK javadoc tool cannot resolve its own
             Kotlin declarations. Generate the javadoc jar with Dokka instead;
             the parent's maven-javadoc-plugin is skipped for this module only.

             When the remaining non-DSL Kotlin is converted to Java, delete this
             profile and let the parent's maven-javadoc-plugin take over again. -->
        <profile>
            <id>release</id>
            <properties>
                <maven.javadoc.skip>true</maven.javadoc.skip>
            </properties>
            <build>
                <plugins>
                    <plugin>
                        <groupId>org.jetbrains.dokka</groupId>
                        <artifactId>dokka-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                        <version>${dokka.version}</version>
                        <executions>
                            <execution>
                                <id>attach-javadocs</id>
                                <phase>package</phase>
                                <goals><goal>javadocJar</goal></goals>
                            </execution>
                        </executions>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirectories>
                                <dir>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</dir>
                                <dir>${project.basedir}/src/main/java</dir>
                            </sourceDirectories>
                            <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                            <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                        </configuration>
                    </plugin>
                </plugins>
            </build>
        </profile>
    </profiles>
</project>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0"
         xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
         xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/xsd/maven-4.0.0.xsd">
    <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

    <parent>
        <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
        <artifactId>pathland-parent</artifactId>
        <version>0.2.2</version>
    </parent>

    <artifactId>pathland-native-core</artifactId>
    <packaging>jar</packaging>

    <name>Pathland Native Core</name>
    <description>
        JNA interop for native desktop hosts: the lazy `PathlandCore` binding to the
        Rust `libpathland_core` cdylib (SPSC ring + opcode engine) and the zero-copy
        `RingOpcodeSink`. Kept out of `pathland-view-core` so server runtimes and
        GraalVM native-image builds never carry JNA. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.
    </description>

    <dependencies>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>dev.pathland</groupId>
            <artifactId>pathland-view-core</artifactId>
            <version>${project.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
            <artifactId>kotlin-stdlib</artifactId>
            <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>net.java.dev.jna</groupId>
            <artifactId>jna</artifactId>
        </dependency>
        <dependency>
            <groupId>org.junit.jupiter</groupId>
            <artifactId>junit-jupiter</artifactId>
            <scope>test</scope>
        </dependency>
    </dependencies>

    <build>
        <plugins>
            <plugin>
                <groupId>org.jetbrains.kotlin</groupId>
                <artifactId>kotlin-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                <version>${kotlin.version}</version>
                <executions>
                    <execution>
                        <id>compile</id>
                        <phase>process-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                    <execution>
                        <id>test-compile</id>
                        <phase>process-test-sources</phase>
                        <goals>
                            <goal>test-compile</goal>
                        </goals>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirs>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/kotlin</sourceDir>
                                <sourceDir>${project.basedir}/src/test/java</sourceDir>
                            </sourceDirs>
                        </configuration>
                    </execution>
                </executions>
                <configuration>
                    <jvmTarget>${maven.compiler.release}</jvmTarget>
                    <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                    <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                </configuration>
            </plugin>
        </plugins>
    </build>

    <profiles>
        <!-- Kotlin-only module: the JDK javadoc tool cannot resolve its own
             declarations, so use Dokka for the Central-required -javadoc.jar. -->
        <profile>
            <id>release</id>
            <properties>
                <maven.javadoc.skip>true</maven.javadoc.skip>
            </properties>
            <build>
                <plugins>
                    <plugin>
                        <groupId>org.jetbrains.dokka</groupId>
                        <artifactId>dokka-maven-plugin</artifactId>
                        <version>${dokka.version}</version>
                        <executions>
                            <execution>
                                <id>attach-javadocs</id>
                                <phase>package</phase>
                                <goals><goal>javadocJar</goal></goals>
                            </execution>
                        </executions>
                        <configuration>
                            <sourceDirectories>
                                <dir>${project.basedir}/src/main/kotlin</dir>
                            </sourceDirectories>
                            <languageVersion>2.4</languageVersion>
                            <apiVersion>2.4</apiVersion>
                        </configuration>
                    </plugin>
                </plugins>
            </build>
        </profile>
    </profiles>
</project>

input.content:
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1
# Multi-stage image for the Pathland Quarkus SSR demo (server-side HTML + /ws deltas).
# Build context is the repository root. The Java path is pure JVM (the HTML
# renderer is a Java port), so the native executable needs no Rust toolchain and
# embeds no native library:
#
#   docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 \
#     -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile -t pathland-quarkus-demo .
#
# Quarkus 3.39 requires GraalVM/Mandrel 25+. Mandrel is the Quarkus-recommended
# GraalVM distribution; the builder image already contains `native-image`.
# The builder image does not ship Maven, so `lib/java/mvnw` is used.

# --- Stage 1: native build with Mandrel ---
FROM quay.io/quarkus/ubi9-quarkus-mandrel-builder-image:jdk-25 AS build

USER root
WORKDIR /src
# The render-html module copies the generated base design from the Rust crate's
# committed assets; no Rust build is needed.
COPY lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets ./lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets
COPY --chown=quarkus:quarkus lib/java ./lib/java
RUN chmod +x lib/java/mvnw

USER quarkus
# Include the extension's deployment module in the reactor: the runtime module's
# quarkus-extension-maven-plugin validates its dependencies against it, and it is
# not a Maven dependency of the demo (so -am alone would omit it).
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/home/quarkus/.m2 \
    cd lib/java && ./mvnw -q -B \
      -pl pathland-quarkus-demo,pathland-quarkus-deployment \

input.content:
# pathland-native-core — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 8, 2026

Opt-in JNA interop for native desktop hosts. Kept in its own module so
`pathland-view-core` (and therefore every server runtime and GraalVM
native-image build) never carries JNA.

## Implemented

- **`PathlandCore`** (`dev.pathland.nativecore`): lazy JNA binding to the Rust
  `libpathland_core` cdylib — ring host lifetime, opcode push, arena allocation,
  frame boundaries, shared ring access, and event drain/send. Resolves the
  library from `pathland.core.lib` or `java.library.path`.
- **`RingOpcodeSink`** (`dev.pathland.nativecore`): zero-copy `OpcodeSink` that
  writes 16-byte opcodes into the Rust SPSC ring through `PathlandCore`,
  including arena-backed strings, design-token paths, float lists, attributed
  text, dates, and theme/window metadata.

## Consumers

- `pathland-desktop-demo` (GTK and Qt hosts) — the only in-repo consumer.
- External native hosts that drive `libpathland_core` directly.

## Not implemented / gaps

- No automated test loads the native library (it is built by `scripts/lib.sh`
  for the desktop demos); the module is compile/test-compile clean without it.

build) carries no JNA.

```
### JVM libraries (`lib/java/`, Kotlin-first)

The reusable JVM library set (`dev.pathland`, Maven reactor, Java 17+) is
Kotlin-authored; the Kotlin DSL serves Spring Boot, Quarkus, and desktop apps:

```

                        #   retained-tree diff emitter, wire codec, router, cross-platform

  pathland-render-html/ # dev.pathland.render.html — the PURE-JAVA HTML renderer:
                        #   a behavioural port of the Rust crate (no JNA, no cdylib), so a
                        #   Maven dependency runs on every platform and under GraalVM

  pathland-server-core/ # dev.pathland.server — transport-agnostic server runtime:

### Native C-ABI shim (`pathland-view-native` + `pathland-core-capi`)

The **desktop/cross-language zero-copy path**: `pathland-view-native` exposes the
flat world (the flat `builder`/`engine` surface) as `pathland_native_*` C
functions with a **shared-memory ring** the host driver reads in place. Any
language that links the dylib (Swift/Java via FFI) calls the flat surface —
no per-component wrappers — and consumes opcodes zero-copy.

`pathland-core-capi` (`libpathland_core`) is the **minimal ring C ABI** for the
Kotlin DSL: `pathland_core_create`/`destroy`, `pathland_ring_buffer_push` (one
raw 16-byte opcode), `pathland_core_arena_alloc`, frame boundaries, zero-copy
`ring_ptr`/`ring_len`, and event drain/send. The Kotlin DSL
(`dev.pathland.view.core.ffm`) binds it with **JNA** (lazily loaded, zero JNI) and
owns the retained tree + diff emission itself.

### GTK4 Renderer (`pathland-render-gtk`)

The desktop renderer: a single crate that owns **all** GTK/glib/pango usage and
maps opcode frames **incrementally** onto native GTK widgets (a retained
`id → gtk::Widget` map). Both the Rust demo and the Java demo render through
it — the demos **never call GTK or Swing directly**:

- Rust demo links `pathland-render-gtk` as an `rlib` and calls `GtkRenderer::run(...)`
  with a wake closure.
- The Java/Kotlin desktop demo (`pathland-desktop-demo`) loads `pathland-render-gtk`
  as a `cdylib` via JNA and
  calls `pathland_gtk_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` over the Kotlin view's
  `libpathland_core` ring; native inputs round-trip as `EVENT` opcodes through the shared
  ring. The renderer **writes** the events and **wakes** the host (no payload); the host
  drains the event ring itself via `pathland_core_drain_events`. Events are never
  delivered through a side-channel callback — they flow through the opcode engine.
---
| Generic RGB | Ambiguous | Explicitly sRGB |
| Hover styles in protocol | Renderer job | Define in theme |
| Heap allocation in steady-state emission | Slow | Preallocated snapshot slab + arena |

---

**Complete**: 16-byte opcode engine (`pathland-core`), SwiftUI-style view DSL with decoupled chainable modifiers (`pathland-view`), declarative diff-based reactive emission (`pathland-core`), **reactive signals** (`pathland-core::signal` — writable `Signal` values bound to node text/properties, so a signal change re-emits only the bound nodes, reachable from Java via the `pathland_native_signal_*` / `node_bind_*` C ABI), host reader to a native-element description (`pathland-render-gtk`), opcode transport with network-batch encode/decode + time/size batching policy (`pathland-core-transport`), golden conformance vectors (incl. raw-input EVENT and network-batch bytes), typed raw-input event encode/decode, `no_std` builds, zero-alloc steady-state emission, the **bidirectional event ring** (host → guest EVENT opcodes in shared memory, drained by the host via a generic `pathland_native_drain_events` C ABI — the renderer only writes + wakes), the **GTK4 renderer** (`pathland-render-gtk`) with Rust demos that render through it without touching GTK directly, the **native JVM library set** — `pathland-view-core` (Kotlin: open `View` interface + shared value/SPI vocabulary, **Angular-parity signals/computed/effects** with synchronous flush, fine-grained retained-tree emitter with **node-level binding effects**, `PLPL` wire codec, router, lazy **JNA ring interop** into `libpathland_core`, cross-platform `StateStore` + **`PersistentState`**) and the sole JVM authoring DSL `dev.pathland.view.dsl` (SwiftUI-shaped builders, modifier sugar, property-delegate state, navigation/media helpers, styles), `dev.pathland.render.html` (pure-Java port of the Rust HTML renderer; input.newString: **Complete**: 16-byte opcode engine (`pathland-core`), SwiftUI-style view DSL with decoupled chainable modifiers (`pathland-view`), declarative diff-based reactive emission (`pathland-core`), **reactive signals** (`pathland-core::signal` — writable `Signal` values bound to node text/properties, so a signal change re-emits only the bound nodes, reachable from Java via the `pathland_native_signal_*` / `node_bind_*` C ABI), host reader to a native-element description (`pathland-render-gtk`), opcode transport with network-batch encode/decode + time/size batching policy (`pathland-core-transport`), golden conformance vectors (incl. raw-input EVENT and network-batch bytes), typed raw-input event encode/decode, `no_std` builds, zero-alloc steady-state emission, the **bidirectional event ring** (host → guest EVENT opcodes in shared memory, drained by the host via a generic `pathland_native_drain_events` C ABI — the renderer only writes + wakes), the **GTK4 renderer** (`pathland-render-gtk`) with Rust demos that render through it without touching GTK directly, the **native JVM library set** — `pathland-view-core` (Kotlin: open `View` interface + shared value/SPI vocabulary, **Angular-parity signals/computed/effects** with synchronous flush, fine-grained retained-tree emitter with **node-level binding effects**, `PLPL` wire codec, router, cross-platform `StateStore` + **`PersistentState`**) and the opt-in `pathland-native-core` (`dev.pathland.nativecore` — lazy **JNA ring interop** into `libpathland_core`, kept off the server classpath) and the sole JVM authoring DSL `dev.pathland.view.dsl` (SwiftUI-shaped builders, modifier sugar, property-delegate state, navigation/media helpers, styles), `dev.pathland.render.html` (pure-Java port of the Rust HTML renderer; golden-fixture-checked byte-for-byte), `dev.pathland.state.redis` (Lettuce `RedisStateStore`, in `pathland-server-core`) — and the **Quarkus demo** (`pathland-quarkus-demo`, a Java host mounting the Kotlin `MusicPlayerView`/`AdView`, plus a Kotlin-only view at `/kotlin`; builds a GraalVM/Mandrel native executable via its Dockerfile), the **desktop demo** (`pathland-desktop-demo`, GTK and Qt), and the **Spring Boot** (`pathland-spring-boot-demo`, a Java host mounting Kotlin views) **SSR + WebSocket demos** with per-window persisted `State` (Redis/in-memory — every browser window/tab gets its own UI model and state scope via a `sessionStorage` window id, so two windows never share a session). **`EVENT_LISTENERS`** (any element emits raw events via a u32 bitmask property) and **`onTapGesture`** (Rust + Kotlin DSL modifier + app-side `TapRecognizer` over the raw pointer events). **Generic input routing** — the emitter returns tap-action / text-input / value-input registries (`RenderResult`), so the host forwards raw `EVENT` batches straight into the bound signals and never reaches into a view's internals. **The media kit** (spec/MEDIA.md) — a non-visual `MEDIA_CONTROLLER` (0x30) state object owning a resource + transport as signals, referenced by a `VIDEO` (0x0A) surface and controlled by the app's own views; # Deploying the Quarkus SSR demo

Runs the [Pathland Quarkus demo](pathland-quarkus-demo/) (server-side HTML at any
path + live `/ws` deltas) as a container — the application evidence for the Restack
proposal (issue #71, `docs/PREAPPLICATION-TODO.md`).

The image is multi-stage: it builds the Java reactor with the Quarkus
Mandrel 25 builder image, compiles the demo to a **GraalVM native executable**
(no JVM at runtime), and copies only the native binary into the UBI9 Quarkus
micro image. No Rust toolchain or native library is needed.

## Requirements

- Docker with BuildKit (or Podman)
- Roughly **6–8 GB RAM** available to the build (native-image is memory-hungry)
- No local GraalVM/Mandrel installation — the builder image provides it
- **x86_64** target (`linux/amd64`); build with `--platform linux/amd64` when
  building on Apple Silicon
- Quarkus 3.39 requires **GraalVM/Mandrel 25+**; the Dockerfile pins the
  `jdk-25` Mandrel builder image

## Build

From the repository root (build context must be the root — the Java reactor plus
the generated base-design assets under
`lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-html/assets/`):

```bash
docker buildx build --platform linux/amd64 \
  -f lib/java/pathland-quarkus-demo/Dockerfile \
  -t pathland-quarkus-demo .
```

The image's Maven step selects both `pathland-quarkus-demo` and
`pathland-quarkus-deployment`. The deployment module is not a Maven dependency of
the demo, but the runtime extension descriptor validates its dependencies against
it; omitting it makes a fresh (empty `~/.m2`) build fail Quarkus extension
verification.

The Mandrel builder image does not ship Maven, so the build uses the committed
`lib/java/mvnw` wrapper. The first build downloads the Maven distribution and all
dependencies; subsequent builds reuse the BuildKit Maven cache. Native
compilation itself typically takes several minutes.

## Run locally

```bash
docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 pathland-quarkus-demo
# → http://localhost:8080
```

A quick check that it serves:

```bash
curl -I http://localhost:8080/          # 200, text/html
curl http://localhost:8080/ | grep -o 'data-pathland-id'   # hydrated SSR markup
curl -sSI https://<host>/ | grep -i '^strict-transport-security'   # HSTS
```

Also verify the native-specific paths:

```bash
curl -I http://localhost:8080/_pathland/assets/audio/track1.mp3   # Range/seek
curl -I http://localhost:8080/_pathland/sw.js                     # Service-Worker-Allowed
curl -I http://localhost:8080/_pathland/base-<hash>.css           # linked base design
curl -sS http://localhost:8080/q/health
curl -sS http://localhost:8080/q/metrics | head
```

The player at `/` embeds the `/ad` app through a same-server `ProxyView`. The
proxy uses the JDK `java.net.http.WebSocket` client; confirm the sponsored slot is
interactive in the native container. If it is not, add
`--initialize-at-run-time=java.net.http,jdk.internal.net.http` to
`quarkus.native.additional-build-args` or switch the Quarkus starter to a
WebSockets Next client.

HSTS is app-owned (the extension does not default it): the demo sets
`max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains` in its `application.properties`. Because
that file is baked into the native image, changing it requires a rebuild/redeploy
— a plain restart of an existing container will not pick it up.

State defaults to the in-memory store (no Redis needed for the demo). To use
Redis, pass a `REDIS_URL` and the Redis `StateStore` in `pathland-server-core` is
selected at runtime. The demo's in-memory path is unaffected by native-image; if
you use Redis with non-JDK state types, add GraalVM serialization reachability
metadata for those types.

## Push to a registry

```bash
docker tag pathland-quarkus-demo ghcr.io/<org>/pathland-quarkus-demo:latest
docker push ghcr.io/<org>/pathland-quarkus-demo:latest
```

## Deploy to a host

Any platform that runs a Docker container exposing TCP 8080 works:

- **Render / Railway / Fly.io** — point at the image (or use a Dockerfile deploy);
  set the public port to **8080**. The app binds `0.0.0.0` (see
  `application.properties`). Build the image for `linux/amd64`.
- **Hetzner / any VPS** — `docker run -d -p 8080:8080 --name pathland pathland-quarkus-demo`
  (optionally behind Caddy/nginx; forward `GET /` and the WebSocket `Upgrade`).
- **Platform port override** — the app honors `QUARKUS_HTTP_PORT` if a platform
  assigns a different port.

### Requirements

- **WebSocket support**: the demo keeps the first page live via `/ws` (raw-input
  events + `PLPL` deltas). The reverse proxy / load balancer must forward the
  WebSocket `Upgrade` headers; most PaaS do this by default.
- **Health check**: `GET /` returning 200 with HTML is the simplest probe. The
  container has no separate health endpoint.
- **Memory**: the native executable has a much smaller footprint than the former
  JVM image (which was capped at `-Xmx256m`); the demo is small.

Quarkus dependency tree still shows JNA via `pathland-view-core:jar:0.2.2` from the local repository (installed old jar with JNA dependency in its POM). We ran `mvn -pl pathland-native-core -am test` which did not install the updated view-core POM to ~/.m2. The dependency tree resolves from ~/.m2 for the reactor? It uses the installed POM. Need to run `mvn install` or use `-am` for the dependency tree. In the actual reactor build, view-core's POM has no JNA. The local ~/.m2 stale POM is causing this. To verify, run `mvn -pl pathland-view-core,pathland-quarkus -am dependency:tree`? The dependency plugin with `-am` will build. Or run `mvn -q -pl pathland-view-core install -DskipTests` then check. But the final build will install. For now, run `mvn -q -pl pathland-view-core -am install -DskipTests` (installs parent, view-core). Then check. Also note the warning about quarkus-junit5 relocated; pre-existing.

Let's install view-core and native-core.
