 # pathland-quarkus — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 7, 2026
 
 Quarkus extension for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding this extension + a
 `PathlandApp` CDI bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at
 their own subpaths (the BFF layout). Author the root view with
 `pathland-view-core`'s Kotlin DSL; Java hosts return Kotlin views from a
 `PathlandApp` bean. The extension also provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus.kotlin`
 capability and pulls in `quarkus-kotlin`.
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Security defaults (issue #63)**: the deployment module contributes
   overridable runtime defaults via `RunTimeConfigurationDefaultBuildItem`:
   `quarkus.http.cors.enabled=true` (no origins → same-origin, which covers
   WebSocket upgrades because the CORS filter runs before routes),
   `quarkus.websockets-next.server.max-message-size`/`max-frame-size=65536`, and
   CSP + `X-Content-Type-Options`/`Referrer-Policy`/`X-Frame-Options` headers via
   `quarkus.http.header.*`. See `docs/HARDENING.md` for overrides, CSP rollout,
   reverse-proxy/TLS guidance, and edge rate limiting. The `wid` handshake query
   is validated by server-core (`WindowIds`). **HSTS is deliberately not an
   extension default** — it is a whole-origin, persistent browser policy that
   also covers other apps on the same server, so it is owned by the application
   or edge; the Quarkus demo opts in via `application.properties`.
   `docs/HARDENING.md` documents the directives and override guidance.
 - **Hosted deployments work by default**: the same defaults set
   `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding`, `allow-x-forwarded`, and
   `enable-forwarded-host` to `true`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS (Render, Fly,
   Heroku, Cloud Run) gets a correct same-origin WebSocket check and an external
   SSR canonical URL with zero configuration. These are lowest-priority defaults;
   application config (including
   `quarkus.http.proxy.proxy-address-forwarding=false`) always wins.
 - **Topic hub bean**: the extension produces a `PathlandSignalHub` singleton
   (`host.signalHub()`: root mount, else the first mount) for external UI updates.
   `TopicSubscriptionsTest` mounts a `/topics` app and proves a background-thread
   publish reaches only the session subscribed for that subject.
 - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `CounterApp` is a Java CDI bean whose
   `newRoot()` returns a Kotlin-authored fixture view; the multi-session
   WebSocket tests prove SSR + live deltas work through that mount.
 
 - **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
 - **SEO document head (issue #45)**: `IndexResource` derives the canonical URL
   from `UriInfo` and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
   `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first
   paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via
   `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.
 
 - **`PathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/_pathland/ws")` for the root app: 1:1 sessions
   per connection (a fresh `uiId` per connection + the client's `wid` state scope from
   the `?wid=` query param), binary events routed into the root registry of the
   `PathlandHost`. **Stateless (critical)**: quarkus-websockets-next endpoints default
   to `@Singleton` — one shared instance for all connections — so the per-connection
   ids come from `connection.id()` + the handshake and the `QuarkusConnection` adapters
   live in a map keyed by connection id. Memoizing `uiId`/`wid`/`transport` on the
   shared instance collapsed every connection onto ONE session (multiple browsers shared
   one UI model — a probe or second tab drove the first tab's session).
 - **`MountedPathlandSocket`** — `@WebSocket("/{app}/_pathland/ws")` for mounted apps:
   the `{app}` path param resolves the app's registry. Mount paths are single-segment.
   Same stateless rule as the root socket.
 - **`IndexResource`** — JAX-RS SSR catch-all (`/` + deep links; `/_pathland/**` and the
   Quarkus non-application root `/q/**` — health/metrics — excluded via negative lookahead)
   dispatching to the longest-mount app (prefix stripped);
   SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS);
   per-app framework files (`/{app}/_pathland/...`, e.g. the mounted app's bundle) are
   served from the shared `/_pathland/**` classpath mount. Quarkus serves the global
   `/_pathland/**` bundle + asset mount from `META-INF/resources` before JAX-RS.
   **The extension jar ships the DOM client bundle** (`META-INF/resources/_pathland/
   dom-renderer-<hash>.js` + the `dom-renderer.current` pointer + the service worker), so
   a consuming application adds the extension and needs no static resources of its own;
   the mounted-base `frameworkFile` path resolves the app's classpath copy first (TCCL),
   then the extension jar, and adds `immutable` caching for the content-hashed bundle. A
   `/_pathland/{file}` JAX-RS route is a fallback for deployments where Quarkus's static
   handler is unavailable (it normally wins).
   **`/_pathland/{name}.css`** (global JAX-RS route + the mounted-base
   `frameworkFile` path) serves the renderer-owned content-hashed base design
   (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
   `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. **`/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg`**
   serves the renderer-owned icon glyphs from the shared Rust renderer
   (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` → `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache
   header — no static CSS/icon files on any host. SSR links the CSS via
   `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
 - **`PathlandRegistryProducer`** — CDI `@Produces @Singleton` `PathlandHost` from every
   `MountedApp` bean plus the lone `PathlandApp` bean (mounted at `/`); `@Disposes` shuts
   it down. Reads the `pathland.debug-html` config property (default `false`) to enable
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output, and `pathland.service-worker` (default `false`)
   to opt the DOM client into the per-window-id service worker (issue #155) — served at
   `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`.
 - **`ServiceWorkerFilter`** — serves `/_pathland/sw.js` (root and mounted bases) with
   `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` + `Cache-Control: no-cache`, so the client's root-scoped
   registration succeeds. A `Filters` handler always runs before routes, so it wins over
   Quarkus's static-resource handler (which sends neither header, and whose configured
   max-age would otherwise cache the script and delay update detection). The script is
   resolved through the thread-context classloader first, then the extension's own
   loader, then the system loader: extension runtime classes live in Quarkus's base
   runtime classloader and cannot see the application's `META-INF/resources` copy. The
   extension jar bundles the worker as a fallback (the TS copy script writes it), and
   `pathland-quarkus-demo`'s integration test asserts the headers on both the root and a
   mounted base — the packaged-app classloader path the module-local test could not see.
 - **Observability (issue #62)** — `quarkus-micrometer` (a `MeterRegistry` bean) +
   `quarkus-smallrye-health`: the producer builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over the
   registry and decorates it with `TracingTelemetry` when a `Tracer` bean is present and
   `quarkus.otel.enabled` (default `true`; the extension never touches the OTel API when
   the extension is absent/disabled). `PathlandHealthCheck` (`@Readiness`) reports the
   host UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/q/health`; the `pathland.*` meters appear
   at `/q/metrics`.
 - **`QuarkusConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketConnection` to `PathlandConnection`.
   Sends are **serialized** (one `sendBinary` subscription in flight, the rest queued),
   and a **send failure closes the connection** so the session drops it and the DOM
   client reconnects + `META::RESYNC` (recoverable) instead of silently stalling on an
   "open" socket that never delivers (the remote seekbar symptom). **Send timeout**: a
   `sendBinary` that neither completes nor fails within 10 s (a half-dead connection /
   a dropped proxy upstream leg) is marked failed and closed — a hung send would
   otherwise wedge the serialized drain forever. **Keep-alive pings**: the connection
   sends a WS-protocol ping every 15 s (browsers auto-pong) to keep the connection warm
   through middleboxes and detect a dead client; `close()` stops the keep-alive
   scheduler (the sockets' `@OnClose` calls it).
 - **Heartbeat** — both sockets reply to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
   **at the transport layer** (through their `QuarkusConnection`, no actor/session
   dependency, and a PING never creates or wakes a session); spec/OPCODE.md
   §Transport heartbeat.
 - **Failure handling** — `fail()` logs the reason; `close()` (socket `@OnClose`)
   no longer calls `close()` on the already-closed connection (no spurious
   "Connection already closed" noise). A **transient write failure on a connection
   that still reports open is logged, not closed** — only a confirmed-dead channel
   (or a send hung past the timeout) warrants closing. The send-timeout task is
   **cancelled when the send completes**, so a completed-but-late callback can't
   false-time-out and kill a healthy connection. Keep-alive pings are sent directly
   (Vert.x serializes writes — no sync with `sendBinary` needed).
 - `META-INF/beans.xml` so Quarkus discovers the extension.
 - **Native image support** — the deployment module registers the renderer-owned
   `dev/pathland/render/html/base.css` + `.name` resources via
   `NativeImageResourceBuildItem`, so `HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` works in a GraalVM
   native executable without app-level `quarkus.native.resources.includes`.
   JNA is not on the server classpath (the ring interop lives in
-  `pathland-native-core`), so native-image builds do not need JNA substitutions.
+  `pathland-native-core`), and Redis/Lettuce is opt-in via
+  `pathland-state-redis`, so the demo's native image carries neither.
   The demo's Dockerfile builds with the Mandrel 25 builder image and runs the
   resulting executable on the UBI9 Quarkus micro image.
 - **Quarkus extension metadata** — runtime + `pathland-quarkus-deployment`; the
   runtime provides the `dev.pathland.quarkus` capability. The runtime has no
   dependency on the authoring DSL. Tests use Kotlin-authored fixture views to prove
   a Java CDI bean can mount them.
 
 ## App DX
 
 ```java
 @ApplicationScoped
 public class MyApp {
     @Produces @Singleton PathlandApp main() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
     @Produces @Singleton MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); }
 }
 ```
 
 ## Verified by
 
 Manual: the `pathland-quarkus-demo` renders `/` (the music player, whose Now
 Playing pane embeds the small `/ad` app via a **same-server `ProxyView`**,
 spec/PROXY.md) and `/ad` (the ad app); a WebSocket handshake to `/_pathland/ws`
 and `/ad/_pathland/ws` returns 101. `ProxyDemoTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts
 `GET /` embeds the `/ad` app's subtree with remapped node ids
 (`data-pathland-id="1073741825"` — proxy block 0 + origin id 1). Core behavior is
 covered by `pathland-server-core` tests. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) opens **100 concurrent real WS
 sessions** against `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar
 probe) and asserts each connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated,
 and is never closed by the peer.
 `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts `/q/health` reports the Pathland
 check UP and `/q/metrics` exposes the `pathland.*` namespace. `BaseCssTest`
 (`@QuarkusTest`) asserts the linked SSR `<link>`, the immutable `text/css`
 response at the global and mounted bases, and a 404 for an unknown hash.

No web-framework dependency — framework glue lives in the starters. ## Implemented - **Security hardening (issue #63)**: `WindowIds` validates the client-supplied `wid` (≤128 chars, `[A-Za-z0-9._-]`; a colon is rejected so it cannot collide with the mount-qualified state scope). The SSR script tag now carries `integrity="sha384-…"` from the manifest's second line (`PathlandAssets.bundleIntegrity()`); an older one-line manifest simply omits it. - **Attributed text transport**: `FrameRebase` rebases `SET_ATTRIBUTED_TEXT`'s string-section offset (like `SET_TEXT`) for delta batching/frame merging, and `ProxyIdMap` remaps its node id. - **Window metadata + SSR head attrs**: `PathlandSession.renderHtml` injects host attrs into the renderer's opening `` (which now carries `lang`), and `FrameRebase` rebases `SET_WINDOW_METADATA` string offsets. Proxy origin metadata is dropped with the other META opcodes. - **Per-route SEO metadata (issue #45)**: `PageMetadata`/`PageMetadataRequest` carry canonical URL, Open Graph/Twitter cards, and JSON-LD. `PathlandApp` gains a default `pageMetadata(request)` hook (active mount-stripped route + host canonical URL); `PathlandRegistry.renderHtml(route, wid, hostDefaults)` merges host defaults with the app's per-route overrides before SSR. Existing overloads keep the legacy head. - **`PathlandApp`** — the app's root-view factory (`View newRoot()` + optional `theme()`); the single app-specific piece a starter needs. - **`MountedApp`** — `record MountedApp(String path, PathlandApp app)`: one app mounted at a subpath prefix (normalized; `/` = root). Hosts any number of them. - **`PathlandHost`** — the multi-app dispatcher: one `PathlandRegistry` per mounted app (own actor thread, own sessions). `match(requestUri)` resolves the owning registry by **longest mount-prefix match** and reports the **mount-stripped route** (a root mount claims every unclaimed path). Duplicate mount paths are rejected at construction. - **`PathlandRegistry`** — session lifecycle per app: single actor thread, 1:1 sessions keyed by a **per-connection `uiId`** (a fresh id per WebSocket connection, so two windows of the same browser never share a UI model), lazy creation on first environment message, pending connections (each carrying the mount-prefixed state scope from the client's per-window `wid`), `open(uiId, wid, conn)`/`environment`/`dispatch`/`resync`/`close`/`renderHtml`/`shutdown`. A Redis/pub-sub-backed hub (each node fanning out to its local sessions) is a follow-up; the topic name + subject are the stable wire keys. - Quarkus mounted-app WebSocket endpoints require a **single-segment** mount path (the `/{app}` path param); Spring supports any depth. ## Proxy views (spec/PROXY.md) — M1 (live) - **`proxy.ProxyIdMap`** — node-id namespacing: the reserved high range `[0x4000_0000, 0x8000_0000)`, 1024 blocks of `2^20`, the block math, and the opcode remap in both directions (`TREE` node ids + the node-id-bearing `PARAMETER` ops `SET_TEXT`/`SET_PROPERTY`/`SET_DATE` on ingress; `EVENT` targets on egress; `META` untouched). `SET_DESIGN_TOKEN` is **not** remapped — its `A` is a token-path arena offset, not a node id (remapping it produced a huge out-of-bounds string offset → the client's RESYNC loop; regression-tested). Pure + unit-tested. - **`proxy.ProxyTransport`** + **`proxy.JdkWebSocketTransport`** — the outbound connection seam (default: the JDK `HttpClient` WebSocket client, no new dependency) with a `Factory` so a starter can swap a native client. - **`proxy.ProxySession`** — one origin connection: sends `META::ENVIRONMENT` + `META::RESYNC`, **remaps** the origin snapshot into the proxy's block and attaches the origin root under the proxy node, forwards live deltas remapped, routes client events back (target unmapped), replies `PONG` to origin `PING`, translates origin `META::RESET` into a **scoped** subtree teardown (never a global reset), tears the subtree down on disconnect (the origin session is per-connection), and reconnects with exponential backoff. While an SSR snapshot is pending, `awaitSnapshot` retries `META::RESYNC` every 500 ms, so a lost first handshake cannot consume the whole SSR budget. The service credential + a cycle-guard instance id ride the handshake headers. **Backpressure** (spec/PROXY.md §8): a "chatty origin" breaker (a per-second batch cap → drop + `RESYNC`) and event coalescing (pointer-moves coalesce by target; discrete events flush immediately). - **`proxy.ProxyHost`** — one `ProxySession` per `PROXY_VIEW` node, each with its own block; routes inbound events whose target is in a proxy range to the owning origin connection; owns the proxy scheduler. `reconcile(wanted)` starts a session for every `PROXY_VIEW` node and closes the session of every node that left the tree; released id blocks go to a **free-block pool** and are reused, so repeated removal/re-add cycles never exhaust the 1024-block range. - **`PathlandSession`** integration — captures `RenderResult.proxyViews()` and registers the emitter's structural-reconcile callback (`Emitter.onStructureReconciled`) to `reconcileProxies()`, so a proxy lives **exactly while its node is in the retained tree** (spec/PROXY.md §7): a `SizeThatFits` slot dropping the candidate that held it closes the origin connection, and re-adding it opens a fresh one (re-seeded by `META::RESYNC`). The host's frames feed the session's `DeltaBatcher` (a single unified sequence); `dispatch` splits proxy-range events to the origin and everything else to the app's own bindings; `close` tears the proxies down. `proxyTransportFactory(...)` lets a host supply a framework transport. - **`PathlandTelemetry`** — `proxyConnected`/`proxyDisconnected`/`proxyBatchDropped`/ `proxyResyncRequested` (all default no-ops). **SSR embed (M2).** `renderHtml` starts the proxies and **blocks** for each origin's snapshot (`ProxySession.awaitSnapshot`, bounded by a 2s timeout), then splices the remapped origin frames into the session's mount frame (`FrameMerger`, reusing the batcher's string rebasing via `FrameRebase`) so the renderer emits **one** document — the origin subtree plus its fit band rules in the same head. The origin's **global** token overrides (`SET_DESIGN_TOKEN`) are **dropped** (live + SSR): a proxied app renders under the **host's** theme, while its token *references* resolve against that theme (spec/PROXY.md §9). A proxy whose origin does not answer in time renders empty (a placeholder) and hydrates over the live connection. A client `META::RESYNC` also replays A's tree **and** asks every origin for a fresh snapshot (`ProxyHost.resyncAll`). **Gaps (M3):** nested proxies and per-proxy theme scoping are deferred (the origin's global overrides are dropped, not scoped, spec/PROXY.md §9). A tiny orphan window remains on removal: an origin batch already queued in the `DeltaBatcher` (≤20 ms) when the proxy node is removed can still create an unattached element in the client's `byId` (not maps, `applyEnvironment`/`resync`/`close` idempotent, registry SSR + lifecycle/teardown, **two windows with the same `wid` still get separate sessions** (a tap to one never reaches the other), and **message-before-open ordering** (environment/resync that race `open` still attach the connection and emit the snapshot). `TopicsTest`: strongly typed `(topic, subject)` routing (customer 43 never sees customer 42's update), every session for a subject updates, global topics reach only subscribed sessions and stay isolated from a same-named scoped topic, rapid publishes coalesce latest-wins, updates run on the session actor, close removes subscriptions, unsubscribe keeps the last value, and a topic outside a session fails on read. `PathlandHostTest`: longest-prefix dispatch + route stripping, mount-boundary respect, no-root-mount 404, per-app base + state scope, duplicate-mount rejection, normalization, SSR emits the mounted app's base. `PathlandTelemetryTest`: a recording telemetry double asserts the registry emits session/event/resync/flush/SSR/close events, the host binds the active-sessions gauge, a failed send reports `connectionFailed`, and `DeltaBatcher` reports the flushed batch. `proxy.ProxyIdMapTest`: the reserved range, block round-trips, overflow rejection, and the opcode remap (TREE/PARAMETER node ids remapped, APPEND/META untouched, EVENT targets unmapped). `proxy.ProxySessionTest` (a fake origin transport): the ENVIRONMENT+RESYNC handshake + handshake headers, snapshot retry when the first RESYNC is lost, snapshot remap + root attachment, delta remap with the string section passed through verbatim, event egress unmapped, pointer-move coalescing, `META::RESET` → scoped teardown, disconnect teardown, and the chatty-origin drop+resync breaker. `proxy.ProxyIntegrationTest`: a `ProxyView` in the app tree opens an origin connection on `connect`, the remapped origin snapshot reaches the client (with the root attached), a client event in the proxy range routes back to the origin unmapped, and the SSR document embeds the origin subtree (remapped ids) in one render. `FrameMergerTest`: splicing a proxy's origin frame into an SSR frame  # pathland-spring-boot-starter — implementation status
 
 **Last updated:** November 7, 2026
 
 Spring Boot auto-configuration for Pathland: SSR at any path, live deltas over each
 app's reserved `/{base}/ws`, per-session state. Adding the starter dependency + a
 `PathlandApp` bean gives a running app; `MountedApp` beans host more apps at their own
 subpaths (the BFF layout).
 
 ## Implemented
 
 - **Security hardening (issue #63)**: the WebSocket handlers no longer hardcode
   `setAllowedOrigins("*")`. The default is Spring's same-origin handshake check
   (the WebSocket CSRF control); cross-origin hosts must be listed explicitly in
   `pathland.allowed-origins` (comma-separated). The handshake `wid` is validated
   by server-core (`WindowIds`). SSR inherits SRI (`integrity="sha384-…"`) from
   `PathlandSession`. CSP/security headers and transport limits are documented in
   `docs/HARDENING.md` (Quarkus supplies secure defaults; Spring apps add them
   through Spring Security/server configuration).
 - **Hosted deployments work by default (issue #45 follow-up)**: a
   lowest-precedence `EnvironmentPostProcessor` contributes
   `server.forward-headers-strategy=framework`, so a TLS-terminating PaaS gets a
   correct WebSocket same-origin check and external SSR canonical URL with zero
   configuration. An explicit `server.forward-headers-strategy` in application
   config always wins (`ForwardedHeaderOverrideTest` pins this).
 - **Topic hub bean**: `PathlandAutoConfiguration` produces a `PathlandSignalHub`
   bean (`host.signalHub()`: root mount, else the first mount) for external UI
   updates. `TopicSubscriptionsTest` mounts a `/topics` app and proves a
   background-thread publish reaches only the session subscribed for that subject.
 - **Java host / Kotlin views**: `KotlinViewMountTest` proves a Java-only
   `@SpringBootApplication` bean returning `PathlandApp` mounts a Kotlin-authored
   fixture view, renders it through SSR, and receives a live signal delta.
 
 - **Crawler endpoints**: `/robots.txt` (text/plain) and `/sitemap.xml` (application/xml) are real routes before the SPA catch-all, so Lighthouse does not parse the HTML shell as robots.txt.
 - **SEO document head (issue #45)**: the SSR controller derives the canonical
   URL from the request and passes host-default `PageMetadata` to the registry;
   `PathlandApp.pageMetadata(...)` may override it per route before the first
   paint. Canonical/OG/Twitter/JSON-LD are on by default and configurable via
   `pathland.seo.{enabled,site-name,image,og-type,twitter-card,twitter-site,structured-data}`.
 
 - **`PathlandAutoConfiguration`** (`@AutoConfiguration`, `@EnableWebSocket` since Spring
   Boot 3.5 no longer auto-enables it) + `META-INF/spring/…/AutoConfiguration.imports`:
-  - default `StateStore` bean (`@ConditionalOnMissingBean` — Redis-or-in-memory),
+  - default `StateStore` bean (`@ConditionalOnMissingBean`, in-memory; add the
+    opt-in `pathland-state-redis` module + a `StateStore` bean for Redis),
   - `PathlandHost` bean (shut down with the context): every `MountedApp` bean plus the
     lone `PathlandApp` bean mounted at `/` (unless an explicit `MountedApp` claims the
     root). Without any app the host is empty and the starter is inert.
   - a `WebSocketConfigurer` registering **one handler per app** at its framework base
     (`/_pathland/ws` for the root, `/{mount}/_pathland/ws` otherwise). Each connection
     gets a fresh `uiId` (its UI model) + the client's `wid` (per-window state scope)
     from the WS `?wid=` query param (kept in `sessionStorage`, never in the page URL),
   - `PathlandIndexController` (SSR catch-all dispatching to the longest-mount app with
     the prefix stripped + a framework static controller serving the bundle + asset mount
     from `classpath:/static/_pathland/**` at both `/_pathland/**` and `/{app}/_pathland/**`;
     the more-specific mapping beats `/{*path}`, and the `!Upgrade` header excludes WS).
     **The starter jar ships the DOM client bundle** (`static/_pathland/dom-renderer-<hash>.js`
     + the `dom-renderer.current` pointer + the service worker), so a consuming application
     adds the dependency and needs no static resources of its own; an app-supplied
     `static/_pathland` copy still wins by classpath order.
     When no static file matches, the controller serves renderer-owned assets from the
     shared Rust renderer: the content-hashed base stylesheet
     (`HtmlRenderer.baseCss()` at `baseCssName()`) as `text/css` with
     `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and
     `/_pathland/icons/{name}.svg` glyphs (`HtmlRenderer.iconSvg` →
     `pathland_html_icon_svg`) with an `immutable` cache header — no static CSS/icon
     files on any host, and a host can still override either with a file. SSR links
     the CSS via `PathlandSession` → `renderLinked`.
     The framework controller honors byte-range requests (`206 Partial Content` +
     `Content-Range`, `416` for unsatisfiable ranges, `Accept-Ranges` on the full
     response) — a `<video>` (a `MediaController`'s playback) seeking beyond its
     buffer issues a `Range`
     request, and answering it with a full `200` would make browsers restart the media
     at byte 0.
     SSR renders defaults (no session cookie — per-window state arrives over the WS).
 - **SSR debug comments**: the host reads the `pathland.debug-html` property
   (`@Value("${pathland.debug-html:false}")`) and forwards it to each registry, enabling
   per-node HTML comments in SSR output when set.
 - **Per-window-id service worker (opt-in, issue #155)**: `pathland.service-worker`
   (default `false`) forwards to the host; the SSR emits `data-pathland-service-worker`
   and the controller serves `{base}/sw.js` with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /` +
   `Cache-Control: no-cache` (a stable, uncached script the browser byte-compares).
 - **`SpringConnection`** — adapts `WebSocketSession` to `PathlandConnection`.
   `AutoCloseable`: a failed send surfaces as a close (the session's
   `closeConnection` closes the underlying session) so the DOM client reconnects +
   `META::RESYNC` instead of silently stalling on an open socket.
 - **Heartbeat** — the socket replies to a client `META::PING` with a `META::PONG`
   **at the transport layer** (through its `SpringConnection`, no actor/session
   dependency; spec/OPCODE.md §Transport heartbeat).
 - **Observability (issue #62)** — `spring-boot-starter-actuator` supplies the
   `MeterRegistry`; auto-config builds a `MicrometerTelemetry` over it (decorated with
   `TracingTelemetry` when an `OpenTelemetry` bean is present — add
   `micrometer-tracing-bridge-otel` to opt in) and a `HealthIndicator` reporting the host
   UP with `activeSessions`/`mounts` at `/actuator/health`. The `pathland.*` meters are
   exposed at `/actuator/prometheus` (add `micrometer-registry-prometheus`).
 
 ## App DX
 
 ```java
 @SpringBootApplication
 public class MyApp {
     public static void main(String[] args) { SpringApplication.run(MyApp.class, args); }
     @Bean PathlandApp pathlandApp() { return () -> new MyHomeView(); }
     @Bean MountedApp support() { return MountedApp.of("/support", ...); } // optional 2nd app
 }
 ```
 
 ## Verified by
 
 `mvn test` — `PathlandAutoConfigurationTest` (`@SpringBootTest`): a `PathlandApp` bean
 mounts at `/` and SSR renders the root. `MultiSessionWebSocketTest`
 (`@SpringBootTest(RANDOM_PORT)`) opens **100 concurrent real WS sessions** against
 `/_pathland/ws` (via the shared `pathland-server-core` test-jar probe) and asserts each
 connects, re-syncs, gets transport-level PONGs, stays isolated, and is never closed by
 the peer. `PathlandObservabilityTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts
 `/actuator/health` reports the `pathland` component UP and the auto-configured
 `PathlandTelemetry` is a `MicrometerTelemetry` registering `pathland.*` meters.
 `BaseCssHeadersTest` (`@SpringBootTest` + `MockMvc`) asserts the linked SSR
 `<link>`, the immutable `text/css` response at the global and mounted bases, and
 a 404 for an unknown hash.
 Manual: the `pathland-spring-boot-demo` renders `/`, `/kitchen`, `/settings`
 and the 404 fallback **and a second app at `/app2`**; a WebSocket handshake to
 `/_pathland/ws` and `/app2/_pathland/ws` returns 101.
\ No newline at end of file

+# pathland-state-redis — implementation status
+
+**Last updated:** November 8, 2026
+
+Opt-in Redis `StateStore` (Lettuce) for the Pathland server runtime. Kept out of
+`pathland-server-core` so deployments that use the in-memory store — and
+GraalVM native-image builds such as the Quarkus demo — never carry Lettuce.
+
+## Implemented
+
+- **`RedisStateStore`** (`dev.pathland.state.redis`): a `StateStore` backed by
+  Lettuce, storing Java-serialized values under plain keys. Supports a default
+  URI (`redis://localhost:6379`), an explicit `RedisURI`, or a caller-supplied
+  `RedisClient`.
+- **`RedisStateStores.redisOrFallback(fallback)`**: probes Redis once and returns
+  the Redis store when reachable, otherwise the supplied fallback (typically
+  `InMemoryStateStore`).
+- **`RedisStateStore.Provider`**: the framework-neutral `StateStoreProvider` SPI.
+- **Native-image metadata**: the module ships
+  `META-INF/native-image/.../native-image.properties`, keeping Lettuce's static
+  Netty DNS resolver holders run-time initialized. Apps that opt into Redis in a
+  native build get the workaround without app-level flags.
+
+## Usage
+
+```java
+@Produces @Singleton
+StateStore stateStore() {
+    return RedisStateStores.redisOrFallback(new InMemoryStateStore());
+}
+```
+
+Add the `pathland-state-redis` dependency and a `StateStore` bean; the Quarkus
+and Spring starters' default in-memory bean yields to it.
+
+## Not implemented / gaps
+
+- Java serialization of non-JDK state types in a native image still needs
+  reachability metadata for those types.
+- No automated Redis integration test (the store requires a live server); the
+  module builds and its provider/fallback seam is testable without one.

parts.text: Add native-image.properties. Use Args with space-separated. Ensure `$` is fine. Write.

input.content:
# Lettuce keeps Netty DNS resolver objects in static fields. Netty marks
# DnsNameResolverBuilder for run-time initialization, while Quarkus initializes
# application classes at build time; GraalVM then rejects the captured resolver
# objects. Keep the three Lettuce holders run-time initialized. This metadata is
# only on the classpath for apps that opt into Redis, so in-memory native builds
# (e.g. the Quarkus demo) never see it.
Args = --initialize-at-run-time=io.lettuce.core.resource.DefaultClientResources \
       --initialize-at-run-time=io.lettuce.core.resource.AddressResolverGroupProvider \
       --initialize-at-run-time=io.lettuce.core.resource.AddressResolverGroupProvider$DefaultDnsAddressResolverGroupWrapper

Framework-agnostic JVM libraries for the Pathland UI protocol: a Kotlin
        authoring DSL with Angular-style signals/computed/effects, a Kotlin opcode
        engine/SPI, the wire codec, a reusable HTML renderer, and cross-platform
        state stores (in-memory by default; the opt-in pathland-state-redis module
        adds Lettuce/Redis). Native desktop hosts use the opt-in JNA ring interop in
        pathland-native-core. Java hosts (Spring Boot, Quarkus, desktop) mount
        Kotlin-authored views. Runs on every LTS from Java 17.

input.oldString:
# --- Native image (GraalVM/Mandrel) ---------------------------------------------
# The starter probes Redis at startup via Lettuce. Lettuce keeps a Netty
# DnsAddressResolverGroup (built from a DnsNameResolverBuilder) in static fields,
# and Netty marks that builder for run-time initialization. Quarkus initializes
# application classes at build time, so those resolver objects would land in the
# image heap and GraalVM rejects them. Keep the three Lettuce holder classes
# run-time initialized; the demo defaults to the in-memory state store, so Redis
# remains optional.
quarkus.native.additional-build-args=--initialize-at-run-time=io.lettuce.core.resource.DefaultClientResources,--initialize-at-run-time=io.lettuce.core.resource.AddressResolverGroupProvider,--initialize-at-run-time=io.lettuce.core.resource.AddressResolverGroupProvider$DefaultDnsAddressResolverGroupWrapper

# --- SEO document head (issue #45) --------------------------------------------

input.content:
# pathland-state-redis — implementation status

**Last updated:** November 8, 2026

Opt-in Redis `StateStore` (Lettuce) for the Pathland server runtime. Kept out of
`pathland-server-core` so deployments that use the in-memory store — and
GraalVM native-image builds such as the Quarkus demo — never carry Lettuce.

## Implemented

- **`RedisStateStore`** (`dev.pathland.state.redis`): a `StateStore` backed by
  Lettuce, storing Java-serialized values under plain keys. Supports a default
  URI (`redis://localhost:6379`), an explicit `RedisURI`, or a caller-supplied
  `RedisClient`.
- **`RedisStateStores.redisOrFallback(fallback)`**: probes Redis once and returns
  the Redis store when reachable, otherwise the supplied fallback (typically
  `InMemoryStateStore`).
- **`RedisStateStore.Provider`**: the framework-neutral `StateStoreProvider` SPI.
- **Native-image metadata**: the module ships
  `META-INF/native-image/.../native-image.properties`, keeping Lettuce's static
  Netty DNS resolver holders run-time initialized. Apps that opt into Redis in a
  native build get the workaround without app-level flags.

## Usage

```java
@Produces @Singleton
StateStore stateStore() {
    return RedisStateStores.redisOrFallback(new InMemoryStateStore());
}
```

Add the `pathland-state-redis` dependency and a `StateStore` bean; the Quarkus
and Spring starters' default in-memory bean yields to it.

## Not implemented / gaps

- Java serialization of non-JDK state types in a native image still needs
  reachability metadata for those types.
- No automated Redis integration test (the store requires a live server); the
  module builds and its provider/fallback seam is testable without one.

Done on branch `feat/quarkus-native-graalvm`.

### What changed

- **JNA split**: new `pathland-native-core` module (`dev.pathland.nativecore`); `pathland-view-core` no longer depends on JNA; desktop demo updated.
- **Redis split**: new opt-in `pathland-state-redis` module (`RedisStateStore`, `RedisStateStores.redisOrFallback`, Lettuce + its native-image metadata). `pathland-server-core` no longer carries Lettuce.
- **Starters**: Quarkus defaults to an `@DefaultBean` in-memory `StateStore`; Spring defaults to in-memory. Apps can override with a `StateStore` bean for Redis.
- **Native resources**: Quarkus deployment registers `base.css` / `base.css.name` via `NativeImageResourceBuildItem`.
- **Native build**: `native` profile, Maven wrapper under `lib/java`, Dockerfile rewritten for Mandrel 25 + UBI9 micro image, x86_64.
- **Cleanup**: removed the temporary Lettuce native-image flags from the demo config.
- Docs/status/AGENTS updated.

### Verified

- `mvn -q -P jvm-only test` passes.
- Release/Dokka profile passes for `pathland-state-redis`.
- Lettuce is absent from `pathland-quarkus` and `pathland-quarkus-demo`; present only in `pathland-state-redis`.
- Native Docker image builds successfully with Mandrel 25:
  - image size ~102 MB
  - startup **0.457 s**
- Native container checks:
  - `/`, `/ad`, `/kotlin` → 200
  - `/_pathland/ws` and `/ad/_pathland/ws` → 101
  - proxied ad subtree present (`data-pathland-id="1073741825"`)
  - audio asset → 200 with `audio/mpeg`
  - `sw.js` → 200 with `Service-Worker-Allowed: /`
  - linked base CSS → 200
  - `/q/health`, `/q/metrics` → 200
